835.g: ਹੋ ਰਮੋ ਤੁਹਾਰੇ ਸਾਥ ਨੀਚ ਕੁਲ ਜਨਮਹਿ ਪਾਊ ॥੩੨॥
835.t: ho ramo tuhaare saath neech kul janameh paauoo ||32||
835.e: ‘But, now, if I ravish with you, I will be reborn in a low caste.’(32)

835.g: ਕਹਾ ਜਨਮ ਕੀ ਬਾਤ ਜਨਮ ਸਭ ਕਰੇ ਤਿਹਾਰੇ ॥
835.t: kahaa janam kee baat janam sabh kare tihaare ||

835.g: ਰਮੋ ਨ ਹਮ ਸੋ ਆਜੁ ਐਸ ਘਟਿ ਭਾਗ ਹਮਾਰੇ ॥
835.t: ramo na ham so aaj aais ghaT bhaag hamaare ||
835.e: (She said,) ‘What are you talking about the birth? They are your concoction..

835.g: ਬਿਰਹ ਤਿਹਾਰੇ ਲਾਲ ਬੈਠਿ ਪਾਵਕ ਮੋ ਬਰਿਯੈ ॥
835.t: bireh tihaare laal baiTh paavak mo bariyai ||
835.e: ‘If you don’t cherish me, then It will be my bad luck.

835.g: ਹੋ ਪੀਵ ਹਲਾਹਲ ਆਜੁ ਮਿਲੇ ਤੁਮਰੇ ਬਿਨੁ ਮਰਿਯੈ ॥੩੩॥
835.t: ho peev halaahal aaj mile tumare bin mariyai ||33||
835.e: ‘Without meeting you, I will poison myself.’(33)

835.g: ਦੋਹਰਾ ॥
835.t: dhoharaa ||
835.e: Dohira

835.g: ਰਾਇ ਡਰਿਯੋ ਜਉ ਦੈ ਮੁਝੈ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਭਗਵਤਿ ਕੀ ਆਨ ॥
835.t: rai ddariyo jau dhai mujhai sree bhagavat kee aan ||
835.e: The Raja was worried, if she imposed the oath of Bhagauti, the Goddess,

835.g: ਸੰਕ ਤ੍ਯਾਗ ਯਾ ਸੋ ਰਮੋ ਕਰਿਹੌ ਨਰਕ ਪਯਾਨ ॥੩੪॥
835.t: sa(n)k tayaag yaa so ramo karihau narak payaan ||34||
835.e: Be will have to ravish her and, then, go to hell.(34)

835.g: ਚਿਤ ਕੇ ਸੋਕ ਨਿਵਰਤ ਕਰਿ ਰਮੋ ਹਮਾਰੇ ਸੰਗ ॥
835.t: chit ke sok nivarat kar ramo hamaare sa(n)g ||
835.e: (She) ‘Get rid of all your doubts, savour me,

835.g: ਮਿਲੇ ਤਿਹਾਰੇ ਬਿਨੁ ਅਧਿਕ ਬ੍ਯਾਪਤ ਮੋਹਿ ਅਨੰਗ ॥੩੫॥
835.t: mile tihaare bin adhik bayaapat moh ana(n)g ||35||
835.e: ‘Because Cupid is over powering me.’(35)

835.g: ਨਰਕ ਪਰਨ ਤੇ ਮੈ ਡਰੋ ਕਰੋ ਨ ਤੁਮ ਸੋ ਸੰਗ ॥
835.t: narak paran te mai ddaro karo na tum so sa(n)g ||
835.e: (Be) ‘How-so-ever Cupid may overwhelm, due to the dread of hell,

835.g: ਤੋ ਤਨ ਮੋ ਤਨ ਕੈਸਊ ਬ੍ਯਾਪਤ ਅਧਿਕ ਅਨੰਗ ॥੩੬॥
835.t: to tan mo tan kaisuoo bayaapat adhik ana(n)g ||36||
835.e: I will never indulge with you.’(36)

835.g: ਛੰਦ ॥
835.t: chha(n)dh ||
835.e: Chhand

835.g: ਤਰੁਨ ਕਰਿਯੋ ਬਿਧਿ ਤੋਹਿ ਤਰੁਨਿ ਹੀ ਦੇਹ ਹਮਾਰੋ ॥
835.t: tarun kariyo bidh toh tarun hee dheh hamaaro ||
835.e: (She) ‘You have been bestowed with youth and I am young too.

835.g: ਲਖੇ ਤੁਮੈ ਤਨ ਆਜੁ ਮਦਨ ਬਸਿ ਭਯੋ ਹਮਾਰੋ ॥
835.t: lakhe tumai tan aaj madhan bas bhayo hamaaro ||
835.e: ‘Seeing you I have overcome with passion.

835.g: ਮਨ ਕੋ ਭਰਮ ਨਿਵਾਰਿ ਭੋਗ ਮੋਰੇ ਸੰਗਿ ਕਰਿਯੈ ॥
835.t: man ko bharam nivaar bhog more sa(n)g kariyai ||
835.e: ‘Abandon all your misconceptions and relish sex with me,

835.g: ਨਰਕ ਪਰਨ ਤੇ ਨੈਕ ਅਪਨ ਚਿਤ ਬੀਚ ਨ ਡਰਿਯੈ ॥੩੭॥
835.t: narak paran te naik apan chit beech na ddariyai ||37||
835.e: ‘And don’t worry about the fear of the hell.’(37)

835.g: ਦੋਹਰਾ ॥
835.t: dhoharaa ||
835.e: Dohira

835.g: ਪੂਜ ਜਾਨਿ ਕਰ ਜੋ ਤਰੁਨਿ ਮੁਰਿ ਕੈ ਕਰਤ ਪਯਾਨ ॥
835.t: pooj jaan kar jo tarun mur kai karat payaan ||
835.e: ‘The lady who comes to me to worship me,

835.g: ਤਵਨਿ ਤਰੁਨਿ ਗੁਰ ਤਵਨ ਕੀ ਲਾਗਤ ਸੁਤਾ ਸਮਾਨ ॥੩੮॥
835.t: tavan tarun gur tavan kee laagat sutaa samaan ||38||
835.e: ‘To me, she is like the daughter of my Guru.’(38)

835.g: ਛੰਦ ॥
835.t: chha(n)dh ||
835.e: Chhand

835.g: ਕਹਾ ਤਰੁਨਿ ਸੋ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਨੇਹ ਨਹਿ ਓਰ ਨਿਬਾਹਹਿ ॥
835.t: kahaa tarun so preet neh neh or nibaaheh ||
835.e: What to talk of love with the women, as they never fulfil,

835.g: ਏਕ ਪੁਰਖ ਕੌ ਛਾਡਿ ਔਰ ਸੁੰਦਰ ਨਰ ਚਾਹਹਿ ॥
835.t: ek purakh kau chhaadd aauar su(n)dhar nar chaaheh ||
835.e: They desert one man and go after another who is better looking.

835.g: ਅਧਿਕ ਤਰੁਨਿ ਰੁਚਿ ਮਾਨਿ ਤਰੁਨਿ ਜਾ ਸੋ ਹਿਤ ਕਰਹੀ ॥
835.t: adhik tarun ruch maan tarun jaa so hit karahee ||
835.e: For whosoever she makes mind for, she becomes naked before him,

835.g: ਹੋ ਤੁਰਤੁ ਮੂਤ੍ਰ ਕੋ ਧਾਮ ਨਗਨ ਆਗੇ ਕਰਿ ਧਰਹੀ ॥੩੯॥
835.t: ho turat mootr ko dhaam nagan aage kar dharahee ||39||
835.e: And immediately presents him her unclad urinary place.(39)

835.g: ਦੋਹਰਾ ॥
835.t: dhoharaa ||
835.e: Dohira

835.g: ਕਹਾ ਕਰੌ ਕੈਸੇ ਬਚੌ ਹ੍ਰਿਦੈ ਨ ਉਪਜਤ ਸਾਤ ॥
835.t: kahaa karau kaise bachau hiradhai na upajat saat ||
835.e: (She, thinking,) ‘What should 1 do to save myself so that my mind is appeased?

835.g: ਤੋਹਿ ਮਾਰਿ ਕੈਸੇ ਜਿਯੋ ਬਚਨ ਨੇਹ ਕੇ ਨਾਤ ॥੪੦॥
835.t: toh maar kaise jiyo bachan neh ke naat ||40||
835.e: ‘Your utterances depict love, how could I kill you.( 40)

835.g: ਚੌਪਈ ॥
835.t: chauapiee ||
835.e: Chaupaee

835.g: ਰਾਇ ਚਿਤ ਇਹ ਭਾਤਿ ਬਿਚਾਰੋ ॥
835.t: rai chit ieh bhaat bichaaro ||

835.g: ਇਹਾ ਸਿਖ ਕੋਊ ਨ ਹਮਾਰੋ ॥
835.t: eihaa sikh kouoo na hamaaro ||
835.e: :By living her my righteousness is destroyed,

835.g: ਯਾਹਿ ਭਜੇ ਮੇਰੋ ਧ੍ਰਮ ਜਾਈ ॥
835.t: yaeh bhaje mero dhram jaiee ||

836.g: ਭਾਜਿ ਚਲੌ ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਦੇਤ ਗਹਾਈ ॥੪੧॥
836.t: bhaaj chalau tiray dhet gahaiee ||41||
836.e: But if I try to run away, she will get me caught.(41)

836.g: ਤਾ ਤੇ ਯਾਕੀ ਉਸਤਤਿ ਕਰੋ ॥
836.t: taa te yaakee usatat karo ||

836.g: ਚਰਿਤ ਖੇਲਿ ਯਾ ਕੋ ਪਰਹਰੋ ॥
836.t: charit khel yaa ko paraharo ||
836.e: ‘It will be better if I praise her and through dramatisation get rid of her.

836.g: ਬਿਨੁ ਰਤਿ ਕਰੈ ਤਰਨਿ ਜਿਯ ਮਾਰੈ ॥
836.t: bin rat karai taran jiy maarai ||
836.e: ‘Without agreeing to commit sex, she will kill me.

836.g: ਕਵਨ ਸਿਖ੍ਯ ਮੁਹਿ ਆਨਿ ਉਬਾਰੈ ॥੪੨॥
836.t: kavan sikhay muh aan ubaarai ||42||
836.e: ‘I wish some disciple of mine could come and save me.’(42)

836.g: ਅੜਿਲ ॥
836.t: aRil ||
836.e: Arril Chhand

836.g: ਧੰਨ੍ਯ ਤਰੁਨਿ ਤਵ ਰੂਪ ਧੰਨ੍ਯ ਪਿਤੁ ਮਾਤ ਤਿਹਾਰੋ ॥
836.t: dha(n)nay tarun tav roop dha(n)nay pit maat tihaaro ||
836.e: (He said to her), ‘You are admirable and so are your mother and father.

836.g: ਧੰਨ੍ਯ ਤਿਹਾਰੇ ਦੇਸ ਧੰਨ੍ਯ ਪ੍ਰਤਿਪਾਲਨ ਹਾਰੋ ॥
836.t: dha(n)nay tihaare dhes dha(n)nay pratipaalan haaro ||
836.e: ‘Your country is commendable and commendable are your sustainers.

836.g: ਧੰਨ੍ਯ ਕੁਅਰਿ ਤਵ ਬਕ੍ਰਤ ਅਧਿਕ ਜਾ ਮੈ ਛਬਿ ਛਾਜੈ ॥
836.t: dha(n)nay kuar tav bakrat adhik jaa mai chhab chhaajai ||
836.e: ‘Your face, which is very pretty, is so meritorious,

836.g: ਹੋ ਜਲਜ ਸੂਰ ਅਰੁ ਚੰਦ੍ਰ ਦ੍ਰਪ ਕੰਦ੍ਰਪ ਲਖਿ ਭਾਜੈ ॥੪੩॥
836.t: ho jalaj soor ar cha(n)dhr dhrap ka(n)dhrap lakh bhaajai ||43||
836.e: ‘That, even, the Lotus- flower, Sun, Moon and Cupid lose their vanity.(43)

836.g: ਸੁਭ ਸੁਹਾਗ ਤਨ ਭਰੇ ਚਾਰੁ ਚੰਚਲ ਚਖੁ ਸੋਹਹਿ ॥
836.t: subh suhaag tan bhare chaar cha(n)chal chakh soheh ||
836.e: ‘Your body is blissful and your eyes are coquettish.

836.g: ਖਗ ਮ੍ਰਿਗ ਜਛ ਭੁਜੰਗ ਅਸੁਰ ਸੁਰ ਨਰ ਮੁਨਿ ਮੋਹਹਿ ॥
836.t: khag mirag jachh bhuja(n)g asur sur nar mun moheh ||
836.e: ‘You are winsome to all, the birds, deer, beasts, reptiles and demons,

836.g: ਸਿਵ ਸਨਕਾਦਿਕ ਥਕਿਤ ਰਹਿਤ ਲਖਿ ਨੇਤ੍ਰ ਤਿਹਾਰੇ ॥
836.t: siv sanakaadhik thakit rahit lakh netr tihaare ||
836.e: ‘Shiva and all his four sons have languished by looking at your eyes.

836.g: ਹੋ ਅਤਿ ਅਸਚਰਜ ਕੀ ਬਾਤ ਚੁਭਤ ਨਹਿ ਹ੍ਰਿਦੈ ਹਮਾਰੇ ॥੪੪॥
836.t: ho at asacharaj kee baat chubhat neh hiradhai hamaare ||44||
836.e: ‘But the strange phenomena is that your eyes have not been able to penetrate into my heart.’(44)

836.g: ਸਵੈਯਾ ॥
836.t: savaiyaa ||
836.e: Savaiyya

836.g: ਪੌਢਤੀ ਅੰਕ ਪ੍ਰਜੰਕ ਲਲਾ ਕੋ ਲੈ ਕਾਹੂ ਸੋ ਭੇਦ ਨ ਭਾਖਤ ਜੀ ਕੋ ॥
836.t: pauaddatee a(n)k praja(n)k lalaa ko lai kaahoo so bhedh na bhaakhat jee ko ||
836.e: (She replied,) ‘Cuddling you I will lie down on the bed and will never divulge this secret to anyone.

836.g: ਕੇਲ ਕਮਾਤ ਬਹਾਤ ਸਦਾ ਨਿਸਿ ਮੈਨ ਕਲੋਲ ਨ ਲਾਗਤ ਫੀਕੋ ॥
836.t: kel kamaat bahaat sadhaa nis main kalol na laagat feeko ||
836.e: ‘Frolicking thus, whole night will pass, and, even the Cupids play will seem trivial.

836.g: ਜਾਗਤ ਲਾਜ ਬਢੀ ਤਹ ਮੈ ਡਰ ਲਾਗਤ ਹੈ ਸਜਨੀ ਸਭ ਹੀ ਕੋ ॥
836.t: jaagat laaj baddee teh mai ddar laagat hai sajanee sabh hee ko ||
836.e: ‘I am living on dreams (about you) and wake up afraid of losing you.

836.g: ਤਾ ਤੇ ਬਿਚਾਰਤ ਹੌ ਚਿਤ ਮੈ ਇਹ ਜਾਗਨ ਤੇ ਸਖਿ ਸੋਵਨ ਨੀਕੋ ॥੪੫॥
836.t: taa te bichaarat hau chit mai ieh jaagan te sakh sovan neeko ||45||
836.e: ‘I would rather die, than to wake up from such a dream.’(45)

836.g: ਦੋਹਰਾ ॥
836.t: dhoharaa ||
836.e: Dohira

836.g: ਬਹੁਰ ਤ੍ਰਿਯਾ ਤਿਹ ਰਾਇ ਸੋ ਯੌ ਬਚ ਕਹਿਯੋ ਸੁਨਾਇ ॥
836.t: bahur tirayaa teh rai so yau bach kahiyo sunai ||
836.e: Then she declared loudly and told, the Raja.

836.g: ਆਜ ਭੋਗ ਤੋ ਸੋ ਕਰੌ ਕੈ ਮਰਿਹੌ ਬਿਖੁ ਖਾਇ ॥੪੬॥
836.t: aaj bhog to so karau kai marihau bikh khai ||46||
836.e: ‘Either I will have sex with you or I will kill myself by taking poison.’(46)

836.g: ਬਿਸਿਖੀ ਬਰਾਬਰਿ ਨੈਨ ਤਵ ਬਿਧਨਾ ਧਰੇ ਬਨਾਇ ॥
836.t: bisikhee baraabar nain tav bidhanaa dhare banai ||
836.e: (Raja,) ‘God has created your eyes like sharp arrows,

836.g: ਲਾਜ ਕੌਚ ਮੋ ਕੌ ਦਯੋ ਚੁਭਤ ਨ ਤਾ ਤੇ ਆਇ ॥੪੭॥
836.t: laaj kauach mo kau dhayo chubhat na taa te aai ||47||
836.e: ‘But He has endowed me modesty and that is why they cannot pierce me.(47)

836.g: ਬਨੇ ਠਨੇ ਆਵਤ ਘਨੇ ਹੇਰਤ ਹਰਤ ਗ੍ਯਾਨ ॥
836.t: bane Thane aavat ghane herat harat gayaan ||
836.e: ‘Your eyes are penetrating and on the very first sight they oust the knowledge.

836.g: ਭੋਗ ਕਰਨ ਕੌ ਕਛੁ ਨਹੀ ਡਹਕੂ ਬੇਰ ਸਮਾਨ ॥੪੮॥
836.t: bhog karan kau kachh nahee ddahakoo ber samaan ||48||
836.e: ‘But for me, having no attraction for sex, they are merely like berries.’(48)

836.g: ਧੰਨ੍ਯ ਬੇਰ ਹਮ ਤੇ ਜਗਤ ਨਿਰਖਿ ਪਥਿਕ ਕੌ ਲੇਤ ॥
836.t: dha(n)nay ber ham te jagat nirakh pathik kau let ||
836.e: (She) ‘Worthy are those berries whom whole world can see,

836.g: ਬਰਬਸ ਖੁਆਵਤ ਫਲ ਪਕਰਿ ਜਾਨ ਬਹੁਰਿ ਘਰ ਦੇਤ ॥੪੯॥
836.t: barabas khuaavat fal pakar jaan bahur ghar dhet ||49||
836.e: ‘And the trees, whose fruit people eat and go home satisfied.’(49)

836.g: ਅਟਪਟਾਇ ਬਾਤੇ ਕਰੈ ਮਿਲ੍ਯੋ ਚਹਤ ਪਿਯ ਸੰਗ ॥
836.t: aTapaTai baate karai milayo chahat piy sa(n)g ||
836.e: Talking nonsensically, she was becoming impatient to meet her love.

836.g: ਮੈਨ ਬਾਨ ਬਾਲਾ ਬਿਧੀ ਬਿਰਹ ਬਿਕਲ ਭਯੋ ਅੰਗ ॥੫੦॥
836.t: main baan baalaa bidhee bireh bikal bhayo a(n)g ||50||
836.e: Her each and every limb was demanding, because she was absolutely stung with the passion.(50)

836.g: ਛੰਦ ॥
836.t: chha(n)dh ||
836.e: Chhand

836.g: ਸੁਧਿ ਜਬ ਤੇ ਹਮ ਧਰੀ ਬਚਨ ਗੁਰ ਦਏ ਹਮਾਰੇ ॥
836.t: sudh jab te ham dharee bachan gur dhe hamaare ||
836.e: The Raja said, "Since I realized I was mature, my Guru has taught:"

836.g: ਪੂਤ ਇਹੈ ਪ੍ਰਨ ਤੋਹਿ ਪ੍ਰਾਨ ਜਬ ਲਗ ਘਟ ਥਾਰੇ ॥
836.t: poot ihai pran toh praan jab lag ghaT thaare ||
836.e: “Aye My Son, so long as there is life m your body,

836.g: ਨਿਜ ਨਾਰੀ ਕੇ ਸਾਥ ਨੇਹੁ ਤੁਮ ਨਿਤ ਬਢੈਯਹੁ ॥
836.t: nij naaree ke saath neh tum nit baddaiyahu ||
836.e: "You promise to enhance love with your own wife."

836.g: ਪਰ ਨਾਰੀ ਕੀ ਸੇਜ ਭੂਲਿ ਸੁਪਨੇ ਹੂੰ ਨ ਜੈਯਹੁ ॥੫੧॥
836.t: par naaree kee sej bhool supane hoo(n) na jaiyahu ||51||
836.e: “But never, even by mistake, bed with else’s wife.(51)

836.g: ਪਰ ਨਾਰੀ ਕੇ ਭਜੇ ਸਹਸ ਬਾਸਵ ਭਗ ਪਾਏ ॥
836.t: par naaree ke bhaje sahas baasav bhag paae ||
836.e: "By relishing another's wife, Inder, the god was showered with female genitals."

836.g: ਪਰ ਨਾਰੀ ਕੇ ਭਜੇ ਚੰਦ੍ਰ ਕਾਲੰਕ ਲਗਾਏ ॥
836.t: par naaree ke bhaje cha(n)dhr kaala(n)k lagaae ||
836.e: "By relishing another's wife, the moon was blemished."

836.g: ਪਰ ਨਾਰੀ ਕੇ ਹੇਤ ਸੀਸ ਦਸ ਸੀਸ ਗਵਾਯੋ ॥
836.t: par naaree ke het sees dhas sees gavaayo ||
836.e: "By relishing another's wife, Ten Headed Raawana lost all his ten heads."

836.g: ਹੋ ਪਰ ਨਾਰੀ ਕੇ ਹੇਤ ਕਟਕ ਕਵਰਨ ਕੌ ਘਾਯੋ ॥੫੨॥
836.t: ho par naaree ke het kaTak kavaran kau ghaayo ||52||
836.e: "By relishing another's wife all the clan of Korav was annihilated." || 52 ||

836.g: ਪਰ ਨਾਰੀ ਸੌ ਨੇਹੁ ਛੁਰੀ ਪੈਨੀ ਕਰਿ ਜਾਨਹੁ ॥
836.t: par naaree sau neh chhuree painee kar jaanahu ||
836.e: "Making love with another's wife is like a sharp dagger."

836.g: ਪਰ ਨਾਰੀ ਕੇ ਭਜੇ ਕਾਲ ਬ੍ਯਾਪਯੋ ਤਨ ਮਾਨਹੁ ॥
836.t: par naaree ke bhaje kaal bayaapayo tan maanahu ||
836.e: "Making love with another's wife is an invitation to death."

836.g: ਅਧਿਕ ਹਰੀਫੀ ਜਾਨਿ ਭੋਗ ਪਰ ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਜੋ ਕਰਹੀ ॥
836.t: adhik hareefee jaan bhog par tiray jo karahee ||
836.e: "Someone who thinks himself to be very brave and indulges carnally with another's wife,"

836.g: ਹੋ ਅੰਤ ਸ੍ਵਾਨ ਕੀ ਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਹਾਥ ਲੇਂਡੀ ਕੇ ਮਰਹੀ ॥੫੩॥
836.t: ho a(n)t savaiaan kee mrit haath leaa(n)ddee ke marahee ||53||
836.e: "He is killed like a dog at the hands of a coward." || 53 ||

836.g: ਬਾਲ ਹਮਾਰੇ ਪਾਸ ਦੇਸ ਦੇਸਨ ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਆਵਹਿ ॥
836.t: baal hamaare paas dhes dhesan tiray aaveh ||
836.e: "Listen my child! Women come to us from far off lands,"

836.g: ਮਨ ਬਾਛਤ ਬਰ ਮਾਗਿ ਜਾਨਿ ਗੁਰ ਸੀਸ ਝੁਕਾਵਹਿ ॥
836.t: man baachhat bar maag jaan gur sees jhukaaveh ||
836.e: "They bow their heads and wish for boons."

836.g: ਸਿਖ੍ਯ ਪੁਤ੍ਰ ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਸੁਤਾ ਜਾਨਿ ਅਪਨੇ ਚਿਤ ਧਰਿਯੈ ॥
836.t: sikhay putr tiray sutaa jaan apane chit dhariyai ||
836.e: "Those Sikhs (disciples) are my sons and their wives are my daughters."

836.g: ਹੋ ਕਹੁ ਸੁੰਦਰਿ ਤਿਹ ਸਾਥ ਗਵਨ ਕੈਸੇ ਕਰਿ ਕਰਿਯੈ ॥੫੪॥
836.t: ho kahu su(n)dhar teh saath gavan kaise kar kariyai ||54||
836.e: “Tell me now, beautiful one, how could I copulate with them." || 54 ||

836.g: ਚੌਪਈ ॥
836.t: chauapiee ||
836.e: Chaupaee

837.g: ਬਚਨ ਸੁਨਤ ਕ੍ਰੁਧਿਤ ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਭਈ ॥
837.t: bachan sunat krudhit tiray bhiee ||

837.g: ਜਰਿ ਬਰਿ ਆਠ ਟੂਕ ਹ੍ਵੈ ਗਈ ॥
837.t: jar bar aaTh Took havai giee ||
837.e: Listening to all this, she flew into rage and thought,

837.g: ਅਬ ਹੀ ਚੋਰਿ ਚੋਰਿ ਕਹਿ ਉਠਿਹੌ ॥
837.t: ab hee chor chor keh uThihau ||

837.g: ਤੁਹਿ ਕੋਪ ਕਰਿ ਮਾਰਿ ਹੀ ਸੁਟਿਹੌ ॥੫੫॥
837.t: tuh kop kar maar hee suTihau ||55||
837.e:
‘Now I should shout, “thief, thief” and people will come and kill
him.’(55)

837.g: ਦੋਹਰਾ ॥
837.t: dhoharaa ||
837.e: Dohira

837.g: ਹਸਿ ਖੇਲੋ ਸੁਖ ਸੋ ਰਮੋ ਕਹਾ ਕਰਤ ਹੋ ਰੋਖ ॥
837.t: has khelo sukh so ramo kahaa karat ho rokh ||
837.e: (She) ‘Why are you getting so angry, jovially have sex with me.

837.g: ਨੈਨ ਰਹੇ ਨਿਹੁਰਾਇ ਕ੍ਯੋ ਹੇਰਤ ਲਗਤ ਨ ਦੋਖ ॥੫੬॥
837.t: nain rahe nihurai kayo herat lagat na dhokh ||56||
837.e: ‘My eyes are inviting you, can’t you understand what they are revealing.’ (56)

837.g: ਯਾ ਤੇ ਹਮ ਹੇਰਤ ਨਹੀ ਸੁਨਿ ਸਿਖ ਹਮਾਰੇ ਬੈਨ ॥
837.t: yaa te ham herat nahee sun sikh hamaare bain ||
837.e: (Raja) ‘Listen, Carefully Listen, I am not looking at you,

837.g: ਲਖੇ ਲਗਨ ਲਗਿ ਜਾਇ ਜਿਨ ਬਡੇ ਬਿਰਹਿਯਾ ਨੈਨ ॥੫੭॥
837.t: lakhe lagan lag jai jin badde birahiyaa nain ||57||
837.e: ‘Because the looks create the feeling of separation.’(57)

837.g: ਛਪੈ ਛੰਦ ॥
837.t: chhapai chha(n)dh ||
837.e: Chhape Chhand

837.g: ਦਿਜਨ ਦੀਜਿਯਹੁ ਦਾਨ ਦ੍ਰੁਜਨ ਕਹ ਦ੍ਰਿਸਟਿ ਦਿਖੈਯਹੁ ॥
837.t: dhijan dheejiyahu dhaan dhrujan keh dhirasaT dhikhaiyahu ||
837.e: ‘Charity is endowed to the priests and the men with base thinking get scornful looks.

837.g: ਸੁਖੀ ਰਾਖਿਯਹੁ ਸਾਥ ਸਤ੍ਰੁ ਸਿਰ ਖੜਗ ਬਜੈਯਹੁ ॥
837.t: sukhee raakhiyahu saath satr sir khaRag bajaiyahu ||
837.e: ‘Friends are entrained with relief and the enemies get hit on the heads with sword.

837.g: ਲੋਕ ਲਾਜ ਕਉ ਛਾਡਿ ਕਛੂ ਕਾਰਜ ਨਹਿ ਕਰਿਯਹੁ ॥
837.t: lok laaj kau chhaadd kachhoo kaaraj neh kariyahu ||
837.e: ‘No act is performed keeping in view the public opinion.

837.g: ਪਰ ਨਾਰੀ ਕੀ ਸੇਜ ਪਾਵ ਸੁਪਨੇ ਹੂੰ ਨ ਧਰਿਯਹੁ ॥
837.t: par naaree kee sej paav supane hoo(n) na dhariyahu ||
837.e: ‘One should not even dream of getting into bed with else’s wife.

837.g: ਗੁਰ ਜਬ ਤੇ ਮੁਹਿ ਕਹਿਯੋ ਇਹੈ ਪ੍ਰਨ ਲਯੋ ਸੁ ਧਾਰੈ ॥
837.t: gur jab te muh kahiyo ihai pran layo su dhaarai ||
837.e: ‘Since the time Guru has taught me this lesson,

837.g: ਹੋ ਪਰ ਧਨ ਪਾਹਨ ਤੁਲਿ ਤ੍ਰਿਯਾ ਪਰ ਮਾਤ ਹਮਾਰੈ ॥੫੮॥
837.t: ho par dhan paahan tul tirayaa par maat hamaarai ||58||
837.e: Any thing belonging to somebody else is like a stone and else’s wife like a mother to me.’(58)

837.g: ਦੋਹਰਾ ॥
837.t: dhoharaa ||
837.e: Dohira

837.g: ਸੁਨਤ ਰਾਵ ਕੋ ਬਚ ਸ੍ਰਵਨ ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਮਨਿ ਅਧਿਕ ਰਿਸਾਇ ॥
837.t: sunat raav ko bach sravan tiray man adhik risai ||
837.e: Listening to the Raja’s talk she became angrier,

837.g: ਚੋਰ ਚੋਰ ਕਹਿ ਕੈ ਉਠੀ ਸਿਖ੍ਯਨ ਦਿਯੋ ਜਗਾਇ ॥੫੯॥
837.t: chor chor keh kai uThee sikhayan dhiyo jagai ||59||
837.e: And shouting, “thief, thief” she awoke all her companions.(59)

837.g: ਸੁਨਤ ਚੋਰ ਕੋ ਬਚ ਸ੍ਰਵਨ ਅਧਿਕ ਡਰਿਯੋ ਨਰ ਨਾਹਿ ॥
837.t: sunat chor ko bach sravan adhik ddariyo nar naeh ||
837.e: Hearing the call of “thief, thief,” the Raja was frightened.

837.g: ਪਨੀ ਪਾਮਰੀ ਤਜਿ ਭਜ੍ਯੋ ਸੁਧਿ ਨ ਰਹੀ ਮਨ ਮਾਹਿ ॥੬੦॥
837.t: panee paamaree taj bhajayo sudh na rahee man maeh ||60||
837.e: He lost his sanity and, leaving there his shoes and silk robe, ran away.(60)

837.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰ ਪਖ੍ਯਾਨੇ ਤ੍ਰਿਯਾ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰੇ ਮੰਤ੍ਰੀ ਭੂਪ ਸੰਬਾਦੇ ਇਕੀਸਵੋ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰ ਸਮਾਪਤਮ ਸਤੁ ਸੁਭਮ ਸਤੁ ॥੨੧॥੪੩੯॥ਅਫਜੂੰ॥
837.t: eit sree charitr pakhayaane tirayaa charitre ma(n)tree bhoop sa(n)baadhe ikeesavo charitr samaapatam sat subham sat ||21||439||afajoo(n)||
837.e: Twenty-first Parable of Auspicious Chritars Conversation of the Raja and the Minister, Completed with Benediction. (21)(439)

837.g: ਦੋਹਰਾ ॥
837.t: dhoharaa ||
837.e: Dohira

837.g: ਸੁਨਤ ਚੋਰ ਕੇ ਬਚ ਸ੍ਰਵਨ ਉਠਿਯੋ ਰਾਇ ਡਰ ਧਾਰ ॥
837.t: sunat chor ke bach sravan uThiyo rai ddar dhaar ||
837.e: When the Raja heard the call, “thief, thief” he became dreadful.

837.g: ਭਜਿਯੋ ਜਾਇ ਡਰ ਪਾਇ ਮਨ ਪਨੀ ਪਾਮਰੀ ਡਾਰਿ ॥੧॥
837.t: bhajiyo jai ddar pai man panee paamaree ddaar ||1||
837.e: He ran out leaving behind his shoes and silk robe.(1)

837.g: ਚੋਰਿ ਸੁਨਤ ਜਾਗੇ ਸਭੈ ਭਜੈ ਨ ਦੀਨਾ ਰਾਇ ॥
837.t: chor sunat jaage sabhai bhajai na dheenaa rai ||
837.e: Hearing the call of thief, all woke up and did not let the Raja runaway,

837.g: ਕਦਮ ਪਾਚ ਸਾਤਕ ਲਗੇ ਮਿਲੇ ਸਿਤਾਬੀ ਆਇ ॥੨॥
837.t: kadham paach saatak lage mile sitaabee aai ||2||
837.e: And within five or seven feet they caught him.(2)

837.g: ਚੌਪਈ ॥
837.t: chauapiee ||
837.e: Chaupaee

837.g: ਚੋਰ ਬਚਨ ਸਭ ਹੀ ਸੁਨਿ ਧਾਏ ॥
837.t: chor bachan sabh hee sun dhaae ||

837.g: ਕਾਢੇ ਖੜਗ ਰਾਇ ਪ੍ਰਤਿ ਆਏ ॥
837.t: kaadde khaRag rai prat aae ||
837.e: Others too heard the call of “thief” and came out with their swords.

837.g: ਕੂਕਿ ਕਹੈ ਤੁਹਿ ਜਾਨ ਨ ਦੈਹੈ ॥
837.t: kook kahai tuh jaan na dhaihai ||

837.g: ਤੁਹਿ ਤਸਕਰ ਜਮਧਾਮ ਪਠੈ ਹੈ ॥੩॥
837.t: tuh tasakar jamadhaam paThai hai ||3||
837.e: People shouted at him and expressed that he should be sent to the hell.(3)

837.g: ਦੋਹਰਾ ॥
837.t: dhoharaa ||
837.e: Dohira

837.g: ਆਗੇ ਪਾਛੇ ਦਾਹਨੇ ਘੇਰਿ ਦਸੋ ਦਿਸ ਲੀਨ ॥
837.t: aage paachhe dhaahane gher dhaso dhis leen ||
837.e: He was rounded up from left, right and all the directions.

837.g: ਪੈਂਡ ਭਜਨ ਕੌ ਨ ਰਹਿਯੋ ਰਾਇ ਜਤਨ ਯੌ ਕੀਨ ॥੪॥
837.t: pai(n)dd bhajan kau na rahiyo rai jatan yau keen ||4||
837.e: Raja did try but he could not find any means (to escape).(4)

837.g: ਵਾ ਕੀ ਕਰ ਦਾਰੀ ਧਰੀ ਪਗਿਯਾ ਲਈ ਉਤਾਰਿ ॥
837.t: vaa kee kar dhaaree dharee pagiyaa liee utaar ||
837.e: People pulled his beard and took his turban off

837.g: ਚੋਰ ਚੋਰ ਕਰਿ ਤਿਹ ਗਹਿਯੋ ਦ੍ਵੈਕ ਮੁਤਹਰੀ ਝਾਰਿ ॥੫॥
837.t: chor chor kar teh gahiyo dhavaik mutaharee jhaar ||5||
837.e: Calling him “thief, thief” they beat him with sticks.(5)

837.g: ਲਗੇ ਮੁਹਤਰੀ ਕੇ ਗਿਰਿਯੋ ਭੂਮਿ ਮੂਰਛਨਾ ਖਾਇ ॥
837.t: lage muhataree ke giriyo bhoom moorachhanaa khai ||
837.e: With the beating of sticks, he fell flat and became unconscious.

837.g: ਭੇਦ ਨ ਕਾਹੂੰ ਨਰ ਲਹਿਯੋ ਮੁਸਕੈ ਲਈ ਚੜਾਇ ॥੬॥
837.t: bhedh na kaahoo(n) nar lahiyo musakai liee chaRai ||6||
837.e: People without understanding the real issue, tied him up with a rope.(6)

837.g: ਲਾਤ ਮੁਸਟ ਬਾਜਨ ਲਗੀ ਸਿਖ੍ਯ ਪਹੁੰਚੇ ਆਇ ॥
837.t: laat musaT baajan lagee sikhay pahu(n)che aai ||
837.e: They were throwing punches and kicks when the Sikhs arrived, too.

837.g: ਭ੍ਰਾਤ ਭ੍ਰਾਤ ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਕਹਿ ਰਹੀ ਕੋਊ ਨ ਸਕਿਯੋ ਛੁਰਾਇ ॥੭॥
837.t: bhraat bhraat tiray keh rahee kouoo na sakiyo chhurai ||7||
837.e: The woman shouted, “brother, brother,” but could not rescue him.(7)

837.g: ਚੌਪਈ ॥
837.t: chauapiee ||
837.e: Chaupaee

837.g: ਜੂਤੀ ਬਹੁ ਤਿਹ ਮੂੰਡ ਲਗਾਈ ॥
837.t: jootee bahu teh moo(n)dd lagaiee ||

837.g: ਮੁਸਕੈ ਤਾ ਕੀ ਐਠ ਚੜਾਈ ॥
837.t: musakai taa kee aaiTh chaRaiee ||
837.e: His face was hit with shoes and hands were tied tightly.

837.g: ਬੰਦਸਾਲ ਤਿਹ ਦਿਯਾ ਪਠਾਈ ॥
837.t: ba(n)dhasaal teh dhiyaa paThaiee ||

837.g: ਆਨਿ ਆਪਨੀ ਸੇਜ ਸੁਹਾਈ ॥੮॥
837.t: aan aapanee sej suhaiee ||8||
837.e: He was put in the jail, and the woman came back to her bed.(8)

837.g: ਇਹ ਛਲ ਖੇਲਿ ਰਾਇ ਭਜ ਆਯੋ ॥
837.t: eeh chhal khel rai bhaj aayo ||

837.g: ਬੰਦਸਾਲ ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਭ੍ਰਾਤ ਪਠਾਯੋ ॥
837.t: ba(n)dhasaal tiray bhraat paThaayo ||
837.e: Through such a deception, the Raja went free and despatched her brother to the prison.

837.g: ਸਿਖ੍ਯਨ ਭੇਦ ਅਭੇਦ ਨ ਪਾਯੋ ॥
837.t: sikhayan bhedh abhedh na paayo ||

838.e: None of the Sikhs could comprehend the mystery and they thought her brother to be a thief.(9)

838.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰ ਪਖ੍ਯਾਨੇ ਤ੍ਰਿਯਾ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰੋ ਮੰਤ੍ਰੀ ਭੂਪ ਸੰਬਾਦੇ ਬਾਈਸਵੋ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰ ਸਮਾਪਤਮ ਸਤੁ ਸੁਭਮ ਸਤੁ ॥੨੨॥੪੪੮॥ਅਫਜੂੰ॥
838.t: eit sree charitr pakhayaane tirayaa charitro ma(n)tree bhoop sa(n)baadhe baieesavo charitr samaapatam sat subham sat ||22||448||afajoo(n)||
838.e: Twenty-second Parable of Auspicious Chritars Conversation of the Raja and the Minister, Completed with Benediction. (22)(448)
Chaupaee

838.g: ਭਯੋ ਪ੍ਰਾਤ ਸਭ ਹੀ ਜਨ ਜਾਗੇ ॥
838.t: bhayo praat sabh hee jan jaage ||

838.e: As the Sun rose, people awoke and went to their respective occupations.
The Raja came out of his palace and seated on his throne.(1)
Dohira

838.g: ਪ੍ਰਾਤ ਭਏ ਤਵਨੈ ਤ੍ਰਿਯਾ ਹਿਤ ਤਜਿ ਰਿਸ ਉਪਜਾਇ ॥
838.t: praat bhe tavanai tirayaa hit taj ris upajai ||
838.e: Next day, early in the morning that lady got up,

838.g: ਪਨੀ ਪਾਮਰੀ ਜੋ ਹੁਤੇ ਸਭਹਿਨ ਦਏ ਦਿਖਾਇ ॥੨॥
838.t: panee paamaree jo hute sabhahin dhe dhikhai ||2||
838.e: And displayed the shoes and the robe publicly.(2)
Chaupaee
The Raja declared in the court that somebody had stolen his shoes and robe.

838.g: ਤਾ ਤੇ ਕਾਲ ਨਿਕਟ ਨਹਿ ਆਵੈ ॥੩॥
838.t: taa te kaal nikaT neh aavai ||3||
838.e: ‘The Sikh, who will find them out for me, will be saved from the clutches of Death.’(3)
Dohira

838.g: ਬਚਨ ਸੁਨਤ ਗੁਰ ਬਕ੍ਰਤ ਤੇ ਸਿਖ੍ਯ ਨ ਸਕੇ ਦੁਰਾਇ ॥
838.t: bachan sunat gur bakrat te sikhay na sake dhurai ||
838.e: Listening to their Guru, the Sikh could not hide (the secret),

838.g: ਪਨੀ ਪਾਮਰੀ ਕੇ ਸਹਿਤ ਸੋ ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਦਈ ਬਤਾਇ ॥੪॥
838.t: panee paamaree ke sahit so tiray dhiee batai ||4||
838.e: And they told about the woman, the shoe and the robe.(4)
Chaupaee
The Raja ordered thus, ‘Go and get her and also bring my shoes and robe.

838.g: ਮੋਰਿ ਕਹੇ ਬਿਨੁ ਤ੍ਰਾਸ ਨ ਦੈਯਹੁ ॥੫॥
838.t: mor kahe bin traas na dhaiyahu ||5||
838.e: ‘Bring her straight to me without reprimanding her.’(5)
Dohira

838.g: ਸੁਨਤ ਰਾਇ ਕੇ ਬਚਨ ਕੋ ਲੋਗ ਪਰੇ ਅਰਰਾਇ ॥
838.t: sunat rai ke bachan ko log pare ararai ||
838.e: Lmmediately, harkening to the Raja, the people hastened to her,

838.g: ਪਨੀ ਪਾਮਰੀ ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਸਹਿਤ ਲ੍ਯਾਵਤ ਭਏ ਬਨਾਇ ॥੬॥
838.t: panee paamaree tiray sahit layaavat bhe banai ||6||
838.e: Brought the woman along with the shoes and the robe.(6)
Arril

838.g: ਕਹੁ ਸੁੰਦਰਿ ਕਿਹ ਕਾਜ ਬਸਤ੍ਰ ਤੈ ਹਰੇ ਹਮਾਰੇ ॥
838.t: kahu su(n)dhar keh kaaj basatr tai hare hamaare ||
838.e: (Raja asked,) ‘Tell me pretty lady, why did you steal my garments?

838.g: ਦੇਖ ਭਟਨ ਕੀ ਭੀਰਿ ਤ੍ਰਾਸ ਉਪਜ੍ਯੋ ਨਹਿ ਥਾਰੇ ॥
838.t: dhekh bhaTan kee bheer traas upajayo neh thaare ||
838.e: ‘Were you not afraid of this group of brave-men (watchmen)?

838.g: ਜੋ ਚੋਰੀ ਜਨ ਕਰੈ ਕਹੌ ਤਾ ਕੌ ਕ੍ਯਾ ਕਰਿਯੈ ॥
838.t: jo choree jan karai kahau taa kau kayaa kariyai ||
838.e: ‘You tell me, the one who commits theft, what should be one’s punishments.

838.g: ਹੋ ਨਾਰਿ ਜਾਨਿ ਕੈ ਟਰੌ ਨਾਤਰ ਜਿਯ ਤੇ ਤੁਹਿ ਮਰਿਯੈ ॥੭॥
838.t: ho naar jaan kai Tarau naatar jiy te tuh mariyai ||7||
838.e: ‘Any way, in consideration of your being a lady, I let you go free, otherwise I would have executed you.’(7)
Dohira

838.g: ਪਰ ਪਿਯਰੀ ਮੁਖ ਪਰ ਗਈ ਨੈਨ ਰਹੀ ਨਿਹੁਰਾਇ ॥
838.t: par piyaree mukh par giee nain rahee nihurai ||
838.e: Her face became pale, and her eyes remained wide open.

838.g: ਧਰਕ ਧਰਕ ਛਤਿਯਾ ਕਰੈ ਬਚਨ ਨ ਭਾਖ੍ਯੋ ਜਾਇ ॥੮॥
838.t: dharak dharak chhatiyaa karai bachan na bhaakhayo jai ||8||
838.e: With extreme heart-palpitation, she was dumbfounded.(8)
Arril

838.g: ਹਮ ਪੂਛਹਿਗੇ ਯਾਹਿ ਨ ਤੁਮ ਕਛੁ ਭਾਖਿਯੋ ॥
838.t: ham poochhahige yaeh na tum kachh bhaakhiyo ||
838.e: (Raja) ‘I am asking you, and you are keeping quiet.

838.g: ਯਾਹੀ ਕੈ ਘਰ ਮਾਹਿ ਭਲੀ ਬਿਧਿ ਰਾਖਿਯੋ ॥
838.t: yaahee kai ghar maeh bhalee bidh raakhiyo ||
838.e: ‘Alright, I will take you to my house, and keeping you comfortably there,

838.g: ਨਿਰਨੌ ਕਰਿ ਹੈ ਏਕ ਇਕਾਤ ਬੁਲਾਇ ਕੈ ॥
838.t: niranau kar hai ek ikaat bulai kai ||
838.e: ‘I will talk to you in seclusion,

838.g: ਹੋ ਤਬ ਦੈਹੈ ਇਹ ਜਾਨ ਹ੍ਰਿਦੈ ਸੁਖੁ ਪਾਇ ਕੈ ॥੯॥
838.t: ho tab dhaihai ieh jaan hiradhai sukh pai kai ||9||
838.e: ‘After that you will be let free.’(9)
Chaupaee
Next morning he called the lady, and talked over whole situation.

838.g: ਤੁਮ ਕੁਪਿ ਹਮ ਪਰਿ ਚਰਿਤ ਬਨਾਯੋ ॥
838.t: tum kup ham par charit banaayo ||

838.e: ‘Getting angry on me you tried to caste a net on me but on the contrary I put you in a dilemma.’(10)

838.g: ਤਾ ਕੋ ਭ੍ਰਾਤ ਬੰਦਿ ਤੇ ਛੋਰਿਯੋ ॥
838.t: taa ko bhraat ba(n)dh te chhoriyo ||

838.e: ‘You were let out on the pretension of my brother,’ the woman presented distinctive reasoning.

838.g: ਬਹੁਰਿ ਐਸ ਜਿਯ ਕਬਹੂੰ ਨ ਧਰਿਯਹੁ ॥
838.t: bahur aais jiy kabahoo(n) na dhariyahu ||

839.e: ‘Never try to attempt such trickery ever again and this time I pardon your transgression.’(11)
Dohira

839.g: ਛਿਮਾ ਕਰਹੁ ਅਬ ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਹਮੈ ਬਹੁਰਿ ਨ ਕਰਿਯਹੁ ਰਾਧਿ ॥
839.t: chhimaa karahu ab tiray hamai bahur na kariyahu raadh ||
839.e: ‘Now, woman, you exonerate me as well, because I don’t want to linger on the dispute.’

839.g: ਬੀਸ ਸਹੰਸ ਟਕਾ ਤਿਸੈ ਦਈ ਛਿਮਾਹੀ ਬਾਧਿ ॥੧੨॥
839.t: bees saha(n)s Takaa tisai dhiee chhimaahee baadh ||12||
839.e: She was, then, endowed a pension of twenty thousand takaas every six months. (12) (1)

839.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰ ਪਖ੍ਯਾਨੇ ਤ੍ਰਿਯਾ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰੋ ਮੰਤ੍ਰੀ ਭੂਪ ਸੰਬਾਦੇ ਤੇਈਸਵੋ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰ ਸਮਾਪਤਮ ਸਤੁ ਸੁਭਮ ਸਤੁ ॥੨੩॥੪੬੦॥ਅਫਜੂੰ॥
839.t: eit sree charitr pakhayaane tirayaa charitro ma(n)tree bhoop sa(n)baadhe teieesavo charitr samaapatam sat subham sat ||23||460||afajoo(n)||
839.e: Twenty-third Parable of Auspicious Chritars Conversation of the Raja and the Minister, Completed with Benediction. (23)(460)
Sortha

839.g: ਦੀਨੋ ਬਹੁਰਿ ਪਠਾਇ ਬੰਦਸਾਲ ਪਿਤ ਪੂਤ ਕਉ ॥
839.t: dheeno bahur paThai ba(n)dhasaal pit poot kau ||
839.e: The father again sent his son to the prison,

839.g: ਲੀਨੋ ਬਹੁਰਿ ਬੁਲਾਇ ਭੋਰ ਹੋਤ ਅਪੁਨੇ ਨਿਕਟਿ ॥੧॥
839.t: leeno bahur bulai bhor hot apune nikaT ||1||
839.e: And, as soon as it was morning, he called him back.(1)
Chaupaee
The Minister started narration and said, ‘My Raja, listen to another anecdote.

839.g: ਤਾ ਤੇ ਤੁਮ ਕੌ ਅਧਿਕ ਰਿਝਾਊ ॥੨॥
839.t: taa te tum kau adhik rijhaauoo ||2||
839.e: I will tell you another Chritar, which will amuse you -2
In a country up in the North, there lived a Raja who belonged to the revered Sun Clan.
Chandra Mati was his principal Rani who was, as if, churned out of milk pudding (3)

839.g: ਏਕ ਸੁਤਾ ਤਾ ਕੇ ਭਵ ਲਯੋ ॥
839.t: ek sutaa taa ke bhav layo ||

839.e: They were blessed with a daughter, who was endowed in their lap by the God Sun, himself.
Her beauty had no bounds  she was like the serenity of the Moon.(4)

839.g: ਜਾ ਸਮ ਔਰ ਨ ਜਗ ਮੈ ਬਾਮਾ ॥
839.t: jaa sam aauar na jag mai baamaa ||
839.e: She was given the name of Sumer Kaur  there was none other like her in the world.
Her beauty prevailed all over the three worlds, as she possessed the Moon like virtues (5)
She was so beautiful that, even, the Cupid ran errands for her.

839.g: ਵਾ ਕੀ ਪ੍ਰਭਾ ਜਾਤ ਨਹਿ ਕਹੀ ॥
839.t: vaa kee prabhaa jaat neh kahee ||

839.e: Her charm could not be explained as she appeared to be like a bouquet of flowers.( 6)
Dohira

839.g: ਜਗੈ ਜੁਬਨ ਕੀ ਜੇਬ ਕੇ ਝਲਕਤ ਗੋਰੇ ਅੰਗ ॥
839.t: jagai juban kee jeb ke jhalakat gore a(n)g ||
839.e: With the awakening of youth, her appendage reflected through her fair complexion,

839.g: ਜਨੁ ਕਰਿ ਛੀਰ ਸਮੁੰਦ੍ਰ ਮੈ ਦਮਕਤ ਛੀਰ ਤਰੰਗ ॥੭॥
839.t: jan kar chheer samu(n)dhr mai dhamakat chheer tara(n)g ||7||
839.e: Like the snowy waves, which jumped up and down in the sea-water.(7)
Chaupaee
She was married to a southern Raja and she started to enjoy variable carnal pleasures.
She gave birth to two sons and a daughter, who were the epitome of splendour as well.(8)

839.g: ਤਿਹ ਸਿਰ ਛਤ੍ਰੁ ਪੂਤ ਬਿਧਿ ਧਰਿਯੋ ॥
839.t: teh sir chhatr poot bidh dhariyo ||
839.e: Soon after that Raja died, the crown of sovereignty was put on the son’s head,

839.g: ਕੋ ਆਗ੍ਯਾ ਤਾ ਕੀ ਤੇ ਟਰੈ ॥
839.t: ko aagayaa taa kee te Tarai ||

839.g: ਜੋ ਭਾਵੇ ਚਿਤ ਮੈ ਸੋ ਕਰੈ ॥੯॥
839.t: jo bhaave chit mai so karai ||9||
839.e: And then whose orders no body could refute and he could do whatever the way he liked.(9)
Long time passed, and the spring season prevailed.

839.g: ਤਾ ਤੇ ਪਿਯ ਬਿਨ ਰਹਿਯੋ ਨ ਪਰੈ ॥
839.t: taa te piy bin rahiyo na parai ||
839.e: She (the widowed Rani) could not bear without her lover
As her heart was riddled with the arrows of separation.(10)
Dohira

839.g: ਬਿਰਹ ਬਾਨ ਗਾੜੇ ਲਗੇ ਕੈਸਕ ਬੰਧੈ ਧੀਰ ॥
839.t: bireh baan gaaRe lage kaisak ba(n)dhai dheer ||
839.e: How could she tolerate and contain herself when the arrows of estrangement pinched her?

839.g: ਮੁਖ ਫੀਕੀ ਬਾਤੈ ਕਰੈ ਪੇਟ ਪਿਯਾ ਕੀ ਪੀਰ ॥੧੧॥
839.t: mukh feekee baatai karai peT piyaa kee peer ||11||
839.e: She talked customarily, but in the heart she was pricked with the for her consort.(11)

840.g: ਸਰ ਅਨੰਗ ਕੇ ਤਨ ਗਡੇ ਕਢੇ ਦਸਊਅਲਿ ਫੂਟਿ ॥
840.t: sar ana(n)g ke tan gadde kadde dhasuooal fooT ||
840.e: The Cupid’s arrows were hitting her and passing straight through,

840.g: ਲੋਕ ਲਾਜ ਕੁਲ ਕਾਨਿ ਸਭ ਗਈ ਤਰਕ ਦੈ ਤੂਟਿ ॥੧੨॥
840.t: lok laaj kul kaan sabh giee tarak dhai tooT ||12||
840.e: She felt the veil of human modesty tearing off.(12)

840.g: ਏਕ ਪੁਰਖ ਸੁੰਦਰ ਹੁਤੋ ਤਾ ਕੌ ਲਯੋ ਬੁਲਾਇ ॥
840.t: ek purakh su(n)dhar huto taa kau layo bulai ||
840.e: She called for a handsome male,

840.g: ਮੈਨ ਭੋਗ ਤਾ ਸੌ ਕਿਯੋ ਹ੍ਰਿਦੈ ਹਰਖ ਉਪਜਾਇ ॥੧੩॥
840.t: main bhog taa sau kiyo hiradhai harakh upajai ||13||
840.e: And had sex with him to her full satisfaction.(13)
Chaupaee

840.g: ਤਾ ਸੌ ਭੋਗ ਕਰਤ ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਰਸੀ ॥
840.t: taa sau bhog karat tiray rasee ||
840.e: He copulated with the woman admirably,

840.g: ਜਨ ਹ੍ਵੈ ਨਾਰਿ ਭਵਨ ਤਿਹ ਬਸੀ ॥
840.t: jan havai naar bhavan teh basee ||
840.e: As if she was his own spouse.
She started to call him every night,
And enjoyed heart felt sex.(14)
Coming there, people saw him and admonished,
And the watchmen reckoned him to be a thief,
Then, the maid would tell a telltale,

840.g: ਤਬ ਗ੍ਰਿਹ ਜਾਰ ਸੁ ਪੈਠੈ ਪਾਵੈ ॥੧੫॥
840.t: tab gireh jaar su paiThai paavai ||15||
840.e: And the paramour would go in.(15)

840.g: ਭੋਗ ਜਾਰ ਸੋ ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਅਤਿ ਕਰੈ ॥
840.t: bhog jaar so tiray at karai ||

840.e: Then, the woman would have sex with the lover,
By adopting various mating styles.(16)
Dohira

840.g: ਜਬ ਚੇਰੀ ਪਹਰੂਨ ਕੋ ਉਤਰ ਦੇਤ ਬਨਾਇ ॥
840.t: jab cheree paharoon ko utar dhet banai ||
840.e: (As a matter of fact) when the maid was talking to the watchman,

840.g: ਤਬ ਵਹੁ ਪਾਵਤ ਪੈਠਬੋ ਮੀਤ ਮਿਲਤ ਤਿਹ ਆਇ ॥੧੭॥
840.t: tab vahu paavat paiThabo meet milat teh aai ||17||
840.e: He had sneaked in to meet her.(17)
Chaupaee
Another night came, the lady called her friend,

840.g: ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਕੋ ਭੇਸ ਧਾਰਿ ਸੋ ਆਯੋ ॥
840.t: tiray ko bhes dhaar so aayo ||
840.e: Disguising himself as a woman, he came in.

840.g: ਇਹ ਬਿਧਿ ਤਾ ਸੋ ਬਚਨ ਉਚਰੇ ॥
840.t: eeh bidh taa so bachan uchare ||
840.e: Then she told him this,

840.g: ਹਮ ਸੋ ਭੋਗ ਅਧਿਕ ਤੁਮ ਕਰੇ ॥੧੮॥
840.t: ham so bhog adhik tum kare ||18||
840.e: ‘You have had enough sex with me.(18)
She said, ‘listen my dear friend,
‘Listen to what I am going to tell you.
And listen with full ear towards me,

840.g: ਅਵਰ ਕਿਸੂ ਤਨ ਭੇਦ ਨ ਦੀਜਹੁ ॥੧੯॥
840.t: avar kisoo tan bhedh na dheejahu ||19||
840.e: ‘On the condition that you never divulge to any one.’(19)

840.g: ਏਕ ਦਿਵਸ ਤੁਮ ਬਨ ਮੈ ਜੈਯਹੁ ॥
840.t: ek dhivas tum ban mai jaiyahu ||
840.e: ‘You go to the woods one day,
And take bath in natural spring water.
(Tell others), ‘I have met Shri Krishna,’

840.g: ਏ ਬਚ ਭਾਖਿ ਮੌਨ ਹ੍ਵੈ ਰਹਿਯਹੁ ॥੨੦॥
840.t: e bach bhaakh mauan havai rahiyahu ||20||
840.e: And then become a silent ascetic.(20)

840.g: ਤੁਮ ਜੋ ਲੋਗ ਦੇਖ ਹੈ ਆਈ ॥
840.t: tum jo log dhekh hai aaiee ||
840.e: ‘The people who would come to see you,

840.g: ਯੌ ਕਹਿ ਯਹੁ ਤਿਨ ਬਚਨ ਸੁਨਾਈ ॥
840.t: yau keh yahu tin bachan sunaiee ||
840.e: ‘You narrate to them.
‘They would, no doubt, indulge in cacophony.
‘Listening to them we would show surprise.(21)

840.g: ਚੜਿ ਝੰਪਾਨ ਸੁ ਤਹਾ ਹਮ ਐ ਹੈ ॥
840.t: chaR jha(n)paan su tahaa ham aai hai ||
840.e: ‘I would come to you sitting in a palanquin,

840.g: ਗੁਰੂ ਭਾਖਿ ਤਵ ਸੀਸ ਝੁਕੈ ਹੈ ॥
840.t: guroo bhaakh tav sees jhukai hai ||
840.e: ‘I would bow to you considering you as my Guru.

840.g: ਲੈ ਤੋ ਕੋ ਅਪਨੇ ਘਰ ਜੈਹੋ ॥
840.t: lai to ko apane ghar jaiho ||
840.e: ‘Then I would bring you to my house,
Ad there we would revel in various sex plays.’(22)
Her friend acted upon the way,
The lady had told him..
(Then) next morning he went into the woods,
And took bath in natural spring water.(23)
Dohira

840.g: ਮਜਨ ਕਰਿ ਬਾਪੀ ਬਿਖੈ ਬੈਠਿਯੋ ਧ੍ਯਾਨ ਲਗਾਇ ॥
840.t: majan kar baapee bikhai baiThiyo dhayaan lagai ||
840.e: After mouth washing, he sat down besides the spring in deep contemplation,

840.g: ਕਹਿਯੋ ਆਨਿ ਮੁਹਿ ਦੈ ਗਏ ਦਰਸਨ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਜਦੁਰਾਇ ॥੨੪॥
840.t: kahiyo aan muh dhai ge dharasan sree jadhurai ||24||
840.e: And declared that Shri Krishna had come into his vision.(24)

841.e: Chaupaee

841.g: ਯੌ ਸੁਨਿ ਲੋਕ ਸਕਲ ਹੀ ਧਾਏ ॥
841.t: yau sun lok sakal hee dhaae ||
841.e: Hearing this the people swarmed to the place,
And with them they brought sweetmeats and snacks
They presented him milk and rice,
And, through numerous ways, paid their obeisance at his feet.(25)
(People said) ‘You had the vision of Krishna,
‘And, thus you have become a prominent Guru.

841.g: ਤਾ ਤੇ ਸਭ ਉਸਤਤਿ ਹਮ ਕਰਹੀ ॥
841.t: taa te sabh usatat ham karahee ||
841.e: ‘Now, as we esteem you very high,

841.g: ਮਹਾ ਕਾਲ ਕੀ ਬੰਦ ਨ ਪਰਹੀ ॥੨੬॥
841.t: mahaa kaal kee ba(n)dh na parahee ||26||
841.e: ‘You emancipate us from the (fear of) death.(26)
Dohira

841.g: ਮਹਾ ਕਾਲ ਕੀ ਬੰਦ ਤੇ ਸਭ ਕੋ ਲੇਹੁ ਛੁਰਾਇ ॥
841.t: mahaa kaal kee ba(n)dh te sabh ko leh chhurai ||
841.e: ‘Please do liberate us from the servitude of the death.

841.g: ਤਵ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਦਿ ਬਿਚਰਹਿ ਸੁਰਗ ਪਰਹਿ ਨਰਕ ਨਹਿ ਜਾਇ ॥੨੭॥
841.t: tav prasaadh bichareh surag pareh narak neh jai ||27||
841.e: ‘We all may, through your benevolence, go to the heaven, and save us from the hell.’(27)
Chaupaee
The hearsay reached the town
And the Rani heard it thoughtfully.
Sitting in palanquin she started to go to that place,
And she took with her twenty-twenty five of her friends.(28)
Dohira

841.g: ਚਲੀ ਚਲੀ ਆਈ ਤਹਾ ਜਹਾ ਹੁਤੇ ਨਿਜੁ ਮੀਤ ॥
841.t: chalee chalee aaiee tahaa jahaa hute nij meet ||
841.e: Walking along she reached the place where there was her friend.

841.g: ਭਾਖਿ ਗੁਰੂ ਪਾਇਨ ਪਰੀ ਅਧਿਕ ਮਾਨ ਸੁਖ ਚੀਤ ॥੨੯॥
841.t: bhaakh guroo pain paree adhik maan sukh cheet ||29||
841.e: Bowing down on his feet, she begged for the peace of mind.(29)
Chaupaee

841.g: ਕਿਹ ਬਿਧਿ ਦਰਸੁ ਸ੍ਯਾਮ ਤੁਹਿ ਦੀਨੋ ॥
841.t: keh bidh dharas sayaam tuh dheeno ||

841.g: ਕਵਨ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਕਰਿ ਕੈ ਗੁਰ ਕੀਨੋ ॥
841.t: kavan kirapaa kar kai gur keeno ||
841.e: ‘You have been endowed with the vision of Siam (Krishna),
‘Please let me listen to your anecdotes to console my heart.(30)
Dohira

841.g: ਜੋ ਕਛੁ ਕਥਾ ਤੁਮ ਪੈ ਭਈ ਸੁ ਕਛੁ ਕਹੌ ਤੁਮ ਮੋਹਿ ॥
841.t: jo kachh kathaa tum pai bhiee su kachh kahau tum moh ||
841.e: ‘Tell me, tell me, whatever transpired between you,

841.g: ਤੁਹਿ ਜਦੁਪਤਿ ਕੈਸੇ ਮਿਲੇ ਕਹਾ ਦਯੋ ਬਰ ਤੋਹਿ ॥੩੧॥
841.t: tuh jadhupat kaise mile kahaa dhayo bar toh ||31||
841.e: ‘How did you meet Krishna, and what boons did he endow.’(31)
Chaupaee
(He replied) ‘I had come here for an ablution, and after’ taking bath I contemplated.

841.g: ਇਕ ਚਿਤ ਹ੍ਵੈ ਦ੍ਰਿੜ ਜਪੁ ਜਬ ਕਿਯੋ ॥
841.t: eik chit havai dhiraR jap jab kiyo ||

841.e: ‘When I sought His divination with great determination, then Shri Krishna came into my vision.(32)

841.g: ਸੁਨੁ ਅਬਲਾ ਮੈ ਕਛੂ ਨ ਜਾਨੋ ॥
841.t: sun abalaa mai kachhoo na jaano ||

841.e: ‘Listen, you the lady in distress, I don’t remember what did he con fen upon me.

841.g: ਮੈ ਲਖਿ ਰੂਪ ਅਚਰਜ ਤਬ ਭਯੋ ॥
841.t: mai lakh roop acharaj tab bhayo ||

841.g: ਮੋ ਕਹ ਬਿਸਰਿ ਸਭੈ ਕਿਛੁ ਗਯੋ ॥੩੩॥
841.t: mo keh bisar sabhai kichh gayo ||33||
841.e: ‘I was astounded with his radiant sight and I lost all my senses.(33)
Dohira

841.g: ਬਨਮਾਲਾ ਉਰ ਮੈ ਧਰੀ ਪੀਤ ਬਸਨ ਫਹਰਾਇ ॥
841.t: banamaalaa ur mai dharee peet basan faharai ||
841.e: ‘With a garland of wild flowers around and yellow clothes on, He came.

‘Krishna’s glamour was so high that, even, the birds, antelopes, and reptiles  idolised him.
‘The deer felt modest and the black-bees went crazy on his lotus-like posture.(35)

841.t: peet basan banamaal mor ko mukaT su dhaarai ||
841.e: ‘The yellow robes, garlands of flowers around the neck and peacock- crown on the head, were exalting.

841.e: ‘With a flute on his mouth, he had the (legendry) jewel of Kaustik (auspiciously churned out of the sea) in his heart.

841.e: ‘He had beautiful bow, elegant quoits and double-edged sword in his hands

841.e: ‘In all his four arms, four hands were ensconed,

841.e: ‘They all had adorned beautiful and novel clothes.’(38)

841.e: (She said) ‘There is no doubt that he was the epitome of Bhagwan,

841.t: eihai uchaarat saasatr sabh ihai bakhaanat bedh ||39||
841.e: And the Vedas and the Shastras stand testimony to that.(39)

842.e: The Minister said, ‘Listen My most cherished Majesty,

842.e: The Raja of Kailakhar had a very pretty lady.

842.t: raaj nasaT ke het tin chit mai kiyaa bichaar ||3||

842.e: Prem Kumari was the name of that Rani.

842.e: One factor always worried her  the Raja had no male issue.( 4)

842.t: putr na gireh yaa ke bhayo biradh gayo havai rai ||
842.e: The Raja had no issue and he was getting old.

842.e: He had lacked sexual potency and was unable to produce a child.(5)

842.t: poot anat kau lai kar pariyai ||

842.e: There was a pregnant lady, which she called to her house.

842.e: She let loose the rumour that the Rani was pregnant.(7)

842.e: She paid lot of money to that lady and bought her son.

842.e: The announcement of the birth of son of Raja gave her immense satisfaction.(8)

842.e: She gave out abundant amounts in alms to the Bards and Minstrels

843.e: And no one realised her deceptive Chritar.(11)(1)

843.e: Now, listen my Raja, I narrate to you the story of a moneylender,

843.e: How a lady in the woods tattooed a bird on his rectum.(1)
Chaupaee

843.g: ਜਬ ਹੀ ਬਨਿਕ ਬਨਿਜ ਤੇ ਆਵੈ ॥
843.t: jab hee banik banij te aavai ||

843.e: Whenever, the moneylender came back (from business), he boasted,
‘1 have killed twenty thieves’.
Some times he would come and say, ‘I have killed thirty thieves.’(2)

843.g: ਸੁਨਿ ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਬੈਨ ਮੋਨ ਹ੍ਵੈ ਰਹੈ ॥
843.t: sun tiray bain mon havai rahai ||
843.e: Every time he bragged as such, wife would just keep quiet.

843.g: ਤਾ ਕੇ ਮੁਖ ਪਰ ਕਛੂ ਨ ਭਾਖੈ ॥
843.t: taa ke mukh par kachhoo na bhaakhai ||

843.g: ਏ ਸਭ ਬਾਤ ਚਿਤ ਮੈ ਰਾਖੈ ॥੩॥
843.t: e sabh baat chit mai raakhai ||3||
843.e: She would not contradict him at his face, and restrained her reaction.(3)

843.g: ਨਿਰਤ ਮਤੀ ਇਹ ਬਿਧਿ ਤਬ ਕਿਯੋ ॥
843.t: nirat matee ieh bidh tab kiyo ||

843.e: Nirat Mati (that lady) devised a scheme and sent for a horse from the stable.
With sword in her hand and a turban on her head, she disguised herself as a man.(4)
With a sword embellishing in her right hand, she would appear to be a soldier,

843.g: ਸਭ ਹੀ ਸਾਜ ਪੁਰਖ ਕੇ ਬਨੀ ॥
843.t: sabh hee saaj purakh ke banee ||

843.e: Dressing herself as a man, she looked like chief of the army.(5)
Dohira.

843.g: ਸਿਪਰ ਸਰੋਹੀ ਸੈਹਥੀ ਧੁਜਾ ਰਹੀ ਫਹਰਾਇ ॥
843.t: sipar sarohee saihathee dhujaa rahee faharai ||
843.e: Bedecked with a sword, a shield, a spear, and a flag, instead of a fernale.

843.g: ਮਹਾਬੀਰ ਸੀ ਜਾਨਿਯੈ ਤ੍ਰਿਯਾ ਨ ਸਮਝੀ ਜਾਇ ॥੬॥
843.t: mahaabeer see jaaniyai tirayaa na samajhee jai ||6||
843.e: She reflected herself to be a great warrior.(6)

843.g: ਬਨਿਜ ਹੇਤ ਬਨਿਯਾ ਚਲਿਯੋ ਅਤਿ ਹਰਖਤ ਸਭ ਅੰਗ ॥
843.t: banij het baniyaa chaliyo at harakhat sabh a(n)g ||
843.e: The moneylender was satisfied in all respects,

843.g: ਗਾਵਤ ਗਾਵਤ ਗੀਤ ਸੁਭ ਬਨ ਮੈ ਧਸਿਯੋ ਨਿਸੰਗ ॥੭॥
843.t: gaavat gaavat geet subh ban mai dhasiyo nisa(n)g ||7||
843.e: And had proceeded jovially towards the woods, singing all the way.(7)
Chaupaee
Seeing him going all alone, she made up her mind to beguile him
Performing fighting feats she came and unleashed the sword.(8)
Dohira

843.g: ਕਹਾ ਜਾਤ ਰੇ ਮੂੜ ਮਤਿ ਜੁਧ ਕਰਹੁ ਡਰ ਡਾਰਿ ॥
843.t: kahaa jaat re mooR mat judh karahu ddar ddaar ||
843.e: ‘Where are you, the fool, going? Come and fight with me,

843.g: ਮਾਰਤ ਹੋ ਨਹਿ ਆਜੁ ਤੁਹਿ ਪਗਿਯਾ ਬਸਤ੍ਰ ਉਤਾਰਿ ॥੯॥
843.t: maarat ho neh aaj tuh pagiyaa basatr utaar ||9||
843.e: ‘Otherwise, taking your turban and clothes away, I will kill you.’(9)
Chaupaee
Hearing this he took his clothes off, and started to nimble the grass (and said),
‘Listen, the swindler, I am your servant, today please pardon and Spare my life.(10)

844.g: ਦੋਹਰਾ ॥
844.t: dhoharaa ||
844.e: Dohira

844.g: ਜੌ ਅਪਨੀ ਤੈ ਗੁਦਾ ਪਰ ਖੋਦਨ ਦੇਇ ਬਿਹੰਗ ॥
844.t: jau apanee tai gudhaa par khodhan dhei biha(n)g ||
844.e: ‘If you let me tattoo a bird on your rectum,

844.g: ਤੋ ਤੁਮ ਅਬ ਜੀਵਤ ਰਹੋ ਬਚੈ ਤਿਹਾਰੇ ਅੰਗ ॥੧੧॥
844.t: to tum ab jeevat raho bachai tihaare a(n)g ||11||
844.e: ‘Only then you can save your life.’(11)

844.g: ਤਬੈ ਬਨਿਕ ਤੈਸੇ ਕਿਯਾ ਜ੍ਯੋਂ ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਕਹਿਯੋ ਰਿਸਾਇ ॥
844.t: tabai banik taise kiyaa jayo(n) tiray kahiyo risai ||
844.e: The moneylender agreed to do whatever the lady said.

844.g: ਥਰਹਰਿ ਕਰਿ ਛਿਤ ਪਰ ਗਿਰਿਯੋ ਬਚਨ ਨ ਭਾਖ੍ਯੋ ਜਾਇ ॥੧੨॥
844.t: tharahar kar chhit par giriyo bachan na bhaakhayo jai ||12||
844.e: He fell flat on his chest and shut his mouth tightly.(l2)

844.g: ਤਬੁ ਤਰੁਨੀ ਹੈ ਤੇ ਉਤਰਿ ਇਕ ਛੁਰਕੀ ਕੇ ਸੰਗ ॥
844.t: tab tarunee hai te utar ik chhurakee ke sa(n)g ||
844.e: Then the lady dismounted the horse and took a knife,

844.g: ਰਾਮ ਭਨੈ ਤਿਹ ਬਨਿਕ ਕੀ ਬੁਰਿ ਪਰ ਖੁਦ੍ਰਯੋ ਬਿਹੰਗ ॥੧੩॥
844.t: raam bhanai teh banik kee bur par khudhrayo biha(n)g ||13||
844.e: As Ram Bhanai (the poet) said, the lady tattooed a bird.(13) (1)

844.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰ ਪਖ੍ਯਾਨੇ ਤ੍ਰਿਯਾ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰੋ ਮੰਤ੍ਰੀ ਭੂਪ ਸੰਬਾਦੇ ਛਬੀਸਮੋ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰ ਸਮਾਪਤਮ ਸਤੁ ਸੁਭਮ ਸਤੁ ॥੨੬॥੫੩੩॥ਅਫਜੂੰ॥
844.t: eit sree charitr pakhayaane tirayaa charitro ma(n)tree bhoop sa(n)baadhe chhabeesamo charitr samaapatam sat subham sat ||26||533||afajoo(n)||
844.e: Twenty-sixth Parable of Auspicious Chritars Conversation of the Raja and the Minister, Completed with Benediction. (26)(533)

844.g: ਚੌਪਈ ॥
844.t: chauapiee ||
844.e: Chaupaee

844.g: ਕੰਕ ਨਾਮ ਦਿਜਬਰ ਇਕ ਸੁਨਾ ॥
844.t: ka(n)k naam dhijabar ik sunaa ||

844.g: ਪੜ੍ਰਹੇ ਪੁਰਾਨ ਸਾਸਤ੍ਰ ਬਹੁ ਗੁਨਾ ॥
844.t: paRrahe puraan saasatr bahu gunaa ||
844.e: There lived one Brahmin named Kanak, who was well versed in Shastras and Puranas.

844.g: ਅਤਿ ਸੁੰਦਰ ਤਿਹ ਰੂਪ ਅਪਾਰਾ ॥
844.t: at su(n)dhar teh roop apaaraa ||

844.g: ਸੂਰ ਲਯੋ ਜਾ ਤੇ ਉਜਿਆਰਾ ॥੧॥
844.t: soor layo jaa te ujiaaraa ||1||
844.e: He was handsome too and, even, the Sun borrowed light from him.(1)

844.g: ਦਿਜ ਕੋ ਰੂਪ ਅਧਿਕ ਤਬ ਸੋਹੈ ॥
844.t: dhij ko roop adhik tab sohai ||

844.g: ਸੁਰ ਨਰ ਨਾਗ ਅਸੁਰ ਮਨ ਮੋਹੈ ॥
844.t: sur nar naag asur man mohai ||
844.e: His attractiveness was so distinguished that the gods, humans, reptiles and demons relished him

844.g: ਲਾਬੇ ਕੇਸ ਛਕੇ ਘੁੰਘਰਾਰੇ ॥
844.t: laabe kes chhake ghu(n)gharaare ||
844.e: His attractiveness was so distinguished that the gods, humans, reptiles and demons relished him

844.g: ਨੈਨ ਜਾਨੁ ਦੋਊ ਬਨੇ ਕਟਾਰੇ ॥੨॥
844.t: nain jaan dhouoo bane kaTaare ||2||
844.e: He had long and wavy hair and his eyes were like those of katara, the killer bird.(2) .

844.g: ਬ੍ਯੋਮ ਕਲਾ ਰਾਨੀ ਰਸ ਭਰੀ ॥
844.t: bayom kalaa raanee ras bharee ||

844.g: ਬਿਰਧ ਰਾਇ ਸੁਤ ਹਿਤ ਜਰੀ ॥
844.t: biradh rai sut hit jaree ||
844.e: There was a Rani by the name of Biyom Kala, whose husband was old and she had no issues.

844.g: ਤਿਨ ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਭੋਗ ਕੰਕ ਸੌ ਚਹਾ ॥
844.t: tin tiray bhog ka(n)k sau chahaa ||
844.e: There was a Rani by the name of Biyom Kala, whose husband was old and she had no issues.

844.g: ਲਏ ਕਪੂਰ ਆਵਤੋ ਗਹਾ ॥੩॥
844.t: le kapoor aavato gahaa ||3||
844.e: As she wished to have sex with Kanak, holding camphor she took him in her arms.(3) . .

844.g: ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਦਿਜਬਰ ਸੋ ਬਚਨ ਉਚਾਰੇ ॥
844.t: tiray dhijabar so bachan uchaare ||

844.g: ਭਜਹੁ ਆਜੁ ਤੁਮ ਹਮੈ ਪਿਯਾਰੇ ॥
844.t: bhajahu aaj tum hamai piyaare ||
844.e: The lady said to the twice born (Brahmm), today you love me.

844.g: ਕੰਕ ਨ ਤਾ ਕੀ ਮਾਨੀ ਕਹੀ ॥
844.t: ka(n)k na taa kee maanee kahee ||

844.g: ਰਾਨੀ ਬਾਹਿ ਜੋਰ ਤਨ ਗਹੀ ॥੪॥
844.t: raanee baeh jor tan gahee ||4||
844.e: Kanak did not heed to her but she took him in her arms.(4)

844.g: ਦੋਹਰਾ ॥
844.t: dhoharaa ||
844.e: Dohira

844.g: ਗਹਿ ਚੁੰਬਨ ਲਾਗੀ ਕਰਨ ਨ੍ਰਿਪਤ ਨਿਕਸਯਾ ਆਇ ॥
844.t: geh chu(n)ban laagee karan nirapat nikasayaa aai ||
844.e: When, holding him, she was kissing him, the Raja walked in.

844.g: ਤਬ ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਕਿਯਾ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰ ਇਕ ਅਧਿਕ ਹ੍ਰਿਦੈ ਸਕੁਚਾਇ ॥੫॥
844.t: tab tiray kiyaa charitr ik adhik hiradhai sakuchai ||5||
844.e: Being ashamed, then, the lady staged a trickery.(5)

844.g: ਯਾ ਦਿਜਬਰ ਤੇ ਮੈ ਭ੍ਰਮੀ ਸੁਨੁ ਰਾਜਾ ਮਮ ਸੂਰ ॥
844.t: yaa dhijabar te mai bhramee sun raajaa mam soor ||
844.e: ‘I had felt some doubt in the intention of this Brahmin,

844.g: ਜਿਨਿ ਇਨ ਚੋਰਿ ਭਖ੍ਰਯੋ ਕਛੂ ਸੁੰਘਨ ਹੁਤੀ ਕਪੂਰ ॥੬॥
844.t: jin in chor bhakhrayo kachhoo su(n)ghan hutee kapoor ||6||
844.e: ‘I was trying to detect the smell of camphor in his mouth.’(6)

844.g: ਸੂਰ ਨਾਮ ਸੁਨਿ ਮੂਰਿ ਮਤਿ ਅਤਿ ਹਰਖਤ ਭਯੋ ਜੀਯ ॥
844.t: soor naam sun moor mat at harakhat bhayo jeey ||
844.e: Hearing this the foolish Raja was satisfied,

844.g: ਸੀਂਘਤ ਹੁਤੀ ਕਪੂਰ ਕਹ ਧੰਨ੍ਯ ਧੰਨ੍ਯ ਇਹ ਤ੍ਰੀਯ ॥੭॥
844.t: see(n)ghat hutee kapoor keh dha(n)nay dha(n)nay ieh treey ||7||
844.e: And started to shower the praises on the lady smelling camphor.(7)(1)

844.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰ ਪਖ੍ਯਾਨੇ ਤ੍ਰਿਯਾ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰੋ ਮੰਤ੍ਰੀ ਭੂਪ ਸੰਬਾਦੇ ਸਤਾਈਸਵੋ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰ ਸਮਾਪਤਮ ਸਤੁ ਸੁਭਮ ਸਤੁ ॥੨੭॥੫੪੦॥ਅਫਜੂੰ॥
844.t: eit sree charitr pakhayaane tirayaa charitro ma(n)tree bhoop sa(n)baadhe sataieesavo charitr samaapatam sat subham sat ||27||540||afajoo(n)||
844.e: Twenty-seventh Parable of Auspicious Chritars Conversation of the Raja and the Minister, Completed with Benediction. (27)(540)

844.g: ਚੌਪਈ ॥
844.t: chauapiee ||
844.e: Chaupaee

844.g: ਅਨਤ ਕਥਾ ਮੰਤ੍ਰੀ ਇਕ ਕਹੀ ॥
844.t: anat kathaa ma(n)tree ik kahee ||

844.g: ਸੁਨਿ ਸਭ ਸਭਾ ਮੋਨਿ ਹ੍ਵੈ ਰਹੀ ॥
844.t: sun sabh sabhaa mon havai rahee ||
844.e: The Minister narrated another story, listening to which whole assembly became silence.

844.g: ਏਕ ਅਹੀਰ ਨਦੀ ਤਟ ਰਹਈ ॥
844.t: ek aheer nadhee taT rahiee ||
844.e: The Minister narrated another story, listening to which whole assembly became silence.

844.g: ਅਤਿ ਸੁੰਦਰਿ ਤਿਹ ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਜਗ ਕਹਈ ॥੧॥
844.t: at su(n)dhar teh tiray jag kahiee ||1||
844.e: A milkman used to live at the bank of a stream; His wife was considered the most beautiful.(1)

844.g: ਦੋਹਰਾ ॥
844.t: dhoharaa ||
844.e: Dohira

844.g: ਰੂਪ ਕੁਰੂਪ ਅਹੀਰ ਕੋ ਸੁੰਦਰ ਤਾ ਕੀ ਨਾਰਿ ॥
844.t: roop kuroop aheer ko su(n)dhar taa kee naar ||
844.e: An ugly looking milkman possessed this pretty wife.

844.g: ਵਹੁ ਤਰੁਨੀ ਇਕ ਰਾਵ ਕੋ ਅਟਕੀ ਰੂਪ ਨਿਹਾਰਿ ॥੨॥
844.t: vahu tarunee ik raav ko aTakee roop nihaar ||2||
844.e: On seeing a Raja, she fell in love with him.(2)

844.g: ਚੌਪਈ ॥
844.t: chauapiee ||
844.e: Chaupaee

844.g: ਦੁਖਤ ਅਹੀਰ ਨਾਰਿ ਕੋ ਰਾਖੈ ॥
844.t: dhukhat aheer naar ko raakhai ||

844.g: ਕਟੁ ਕਟੁ ਬਚਨ ਰੈਨ ਦਿਨ ਭਾਖੈ ॥
844.t: kaT kaT bachan rain dhin bhaakhai ||
844.e: The milkman had kept the woman under distress and, day in and day out, used to beat her.

844.g: ਗੋਰਸ ਬੇਚਨ ਜਾਨ ਨ ਦੇਈ ॥
844.t: goras bechan jaan na dheiee ||
844.e: The milkman had kept the woman under distress and, day in and day out, used to beat her.

844.g: ਛੀਨਿ ਬੇਚਿ ਗਹਨਨ ਕਹ ਲਈ ॥੩॥
844.t: chheen bech gahanan keh liee ||3||
844.e: He would not let her go to sell even the milk and he had snatched her ornaments and sold them.(3)

844.g: ਅੜਿਲ ॥
844.t: aRil ||
844.e: Arril

844.g: ਸੂਰਛਟ ਤਿਹ ਨਾਮ ਤਰੁਨਿ ਕੋ ਜਾਨਿਯੈ ॥
844.t: soorachhaT teh naam tarun ko jaaniyai ||

845.g: ਛਤ੍ਰ ਕੇਤੁ ਨ੍ਰਿਪ ਭਏ ਅਧਿਕ ਹਿਤ ਮਾਨਿਯੈ ॥
845.t: chhatr ket nirap bhe adhik hit maaniyai ||
845.e: She was known as Soorchhat and name of the Raja was Chatarket.

845.g: ਚੰਦ੍ਰਭਗਾ ਸਰਿਤਾ ਤਟ ਭੈਸ ਚਰਾਵਈ ॥
845.t: cha(n)dhrabhagaa saritaa taT bhais charaaviee ||
845.e: The buffaloes were grazed at the banks of the Chandrabhaga Stream

845.g: ਹੋ ਜਹੀ ਰਾਵ ਨਾਵਨ ਹਿਤ ਨਿਤਪ੍ਰਤ ਆਵਈ ॥੪॥
845.t: ho jahee raav naavan hit nitaprat aaviee ||4||
845.e: And the Raja used to come to bathe himself there.(4)

845.g: ਚੌਪਈ ॥
845.t: chauapiee ||
845.e: Chaupaee

845.g: ਗੋਰਸ ਦੁਹਨ ਤ੍ਰਿਯਹਿ ਤਹ ਲ੍ਯਾਵੈ ॥
845.t: goras dhuhan tirayeh teh layaavai ||

845.g: ਸਮੈ ਪਾਇ ਰਾਜਾ ਤਹ ਜਾਵੈ ॥
845.t: samai pai raajaa teh jaavai ||
845.e: She used to bring buffaloes there for milking and at the same time Raja would reach there as well.

845.g: ਦੁਹਤ ਛੀਰਿ ਕਟਿਯਾ ਦੁਖ ਦੇਈ ॥
845.t: dhuhat chheer kaTiyaa dhukh dheiee ||
845.e: She used to bring buffaloes there for milking and at the same time Raja would reach there as well.

845.g: ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਕਹ ਭਾਖਿ ਤਾਹਿ ਗਹਿ ਲੇਈ ॥੫॥
845.t: tiray keh bhaakh taeh geh leiee ||5||
845.e: Whenever the calf troubled the milk-man, he used to call her to hold it (the calf).(5)

845.g: ਦੋਹਰਾ ॥
845.t: dhoharaa ||
845.e: Dohira

845.g: ਜਬ ਵਹੁ ਚੋਵਤ ਭੈਸ ਕੋ ਕਰਿ ਕੈ ਨੀਚਾ ਸੀਸ ॥
845.t: jab vahu chovat bhais ko kar kai neechaa sees ||
845.e: Whenever the milkman hung his head down to milk,

845.g: ਤੁਰਤ ਆਨਿ ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਕੋ ਭਜੈ ਬਹੁ ਪੁਰਖਨ ਕੋ ਈਸ ॥੬॥
845.t: turat aan tiray ko bhajai bahu purakhan ko iees ||6||
845.e: The Raja would come immediately and fumble the woman (6)

845.g: ਭਾਤਿ ਭਾਤਿ ਰਾਜਾ ਭਜੈ ਤਾ ਕਹ ਮੋਦ ਬਢਾਇ ॥
845.t: bhaat bhaat raajaa bhajai taa keh modh baddai ||
845.e: The Raja would revel valiantly and enjoy the pleasure.

845.g: ਚਿਮਟਿ ਚਿਮਟਿ ਸੁੰਦਰਿ ਰਮੈ ਲਪਟਿ ਲਪਟਿ ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਜਾਇ ॥੭॥
845.t: chimaT chimaT su(n)dhar ramai lapaT lapaT tiray jai ||7||
845.e: By hugging exquisitely, she would relish as well.(7)

845.g: ਚੋਟ ਲਗੇ ਮਹਿਖੀ ਕੰਪੈ ਦੁਘਦ ਪਰਤ ਛਿਤ ਆਇ ॥
845.t: choT lage mahikhee ka(n)pai dhughadh parat chhit aai ||
845.e: When hurt, the buffalo would jerk and milk would spill,

845.g: ਸੰਗ ਅਹੀਰ ਅਹੀਰਨੀ ਬੋਲਤ ਕੋਪ ਬਢਾਇ ॥੮॥
845.t: sa(n)g aheer aheeranee bolat kop baddai ||8||
845.e: The milkman would rebuke her in anger.(8)

845.g: ਅੜਿਲ ॥
845.t: aRil ||
845.e: Arril

848.g: ਆਜੁ ਭਜਹੁ ਮੁਹਿ ਆਨਿ ਪ੍ਯਾਰੇ ॥
848.t: aaj bhajahu muh aan payaare ||
848.e: The Woman requested him to come that day to make love.

848.g: ਤਿਨ ਵਾ ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਸੌ ਭੋਗ ਨ ਕਰਿਯੋ ॥
848.t: tin vaa tiray sau bhog na kariyo ||

848.g: ਰਾਮ ਨਾਮ ਲੈ ਉਰ ਮੈ ਧਰਿਯੋ ॥੪॥
848.t: raam naam lai ur mai dhariyo ||4||
848.e: He indulged in sex with the woman but, then, recollected the Godly Name.(4)

848.g: ਦੋਹਰਾ ॥
848.t: dhoharaa ||
848.e: Dohira

848.g: ਰਾਮ ਨਾਮ ਲੈ ਉਠਿ ਚਲਾ ਜਾਤ ਨਿਹਾਰਾ ਨਾਰਿ ॥
848.t: raam naam lai uTh chalaa jaat nihaaraa naar ||
848.e: After remembering the Godly Name, he tried to sneak out,

848.g: ਚੋਰ ਚੋਰ ਕਹਿ ਕੈ ਉਠੀ ਅਤਿ ਚਿਤ ਕੋਪ ਬਿਚਾਰ ॥੫॥
848.t: chor chor keh kai uThee at chit kop bichaar ||5||
848.e: She flew into rage and shouted, ‘thief, thief.’(5)

848.g: ਸੁਨਤ ਚੋਰ ਕੋ ਬਚ ਸ੍ਰਵਨ ਲੋਕ ਪਹੁੰਚੈ ਆਇ ॥
848.t: sunat chor ko bach sravan lok pahu(n)chai aai ||
848.e: Listening the call, ‘thief, thief,’ people barged in.

848.g: ਬੰਦਸਾਲ ਭੀਤਰ ਤਿਸੈ ਤਦ ਹੀ ਦਿਯਾ ਪਠਾਇ ॥੬॥
848.t: ba(n)dhasaal bheetar tisai tadh hee dhiyaa paThai ||6||
848.e: He was caught and put in the prison.(6)

848.g: ਤਦ ਲੌ ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਕੁਟਵਾਰ ਕੇ ਭਈ ਪੁਕਾਰੂ ਜਾਇ ॥
848.t: tadh lau tiray kuTavaar ke bhiee pukaaroo jai ||
848.e: That is how a woman by shouting got (the man) beaten,

848.g: ਧਨ ਬਲ ਤੇ ਤਿਹ ਸਾਧ ਕਹ ਜਮਪੁਰਿ ਦਯੋ ਪਠਾਇ ॥੭॥
848.t: dhan bal te teh saadh keh jamapur dhayo paThai ||7||
848.e: And on the strength of wealth got that innocent man punished.(7)

848.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰ ਪਖ੍ਯਾਨੇ ਤ੍ਰਿਯਾ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰੋ ਮੰਤ੍ਰੀ ਭੂਪ ਸੰਬਾਦੇ ਇਕਤੀਸਵੋ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰ ਸਮਾਪਤਮ ਸਤੁ ਸੁਭਮ ਸਤੁ ॥੩੧॥੬੦੫॥ਅਫਜੂੰ॥
848.t: eit sree charitr pakhayaane tirayaa charitro ma(n)tree bhoop sa(n)baadhe ikateesavo charitr samaapatam sat subham sat ||31||605||afajoo(n)||
848.e: Thirty-first Parable of Auspicious Chritars Conversation of the Raja and the Minister Completed with Benediction. (31)(605)

848.g: ਚੌਪਈ ॥
848.t: chauapiee ||
848.e: Chaupaee

848.g: ਸੁਨਹੁ ਨ੍ਰਿਪਤਿ ਇਕ ਕਥਾ ਸੁਨਾਊ ॥
848.t: sunahu nirapat ik kathaa sunaauoo ||

848.g: ਤਾ ਤੇ ਤੁਮ ਕਹ ਅਧਿਕ ਰਿਝਾਊ ॥
848.t: taa te tum keh adhik rijhaauoo ||
848.e: Listen, my Raja, I relate to you one tale, which will provide tremendous relief

848.g: ਦੇਸ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਏਕ ਬਰ ਨਾਰੀ ॥
848.t: dhes pa(n)jaab ek bar naaree ||

848.g: ਚੰਦ੍ਰ ਲਈ ਜਾ ਤੇ ਉਜਿਯਾਰੀ ॥੧॥
848.t: cha(n)dhr liee jaa te ujiyaaree ||1||
848.e: In the country of Punjab, there lived a woman from whom the Moon had acquired its brilliance.(1)

848.g: ਰਸ ਮੰਜਰੀ ਨਾਮ ਤਿਹ ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਕੋ ॥
848.t: ras ma(n)jaree naam teh tiray ko ||
848.e: In the country of Punjab, there lived a woman from whom the Moon had acquired its brilliance.(1)

848.g: ਨਿਰਖਿ ਪ੍ਰਭਾ ਲਾਗਤ ਸੁਖ ਜਿਯ ਕੋ ॥
848.t: nirakh prabhaa laagat sukh jiy ko ||
848.e: Ras Manjri was her name and on seeing her one’s mind attained bliss.

848.g: ਤਾ ਕੋ ਨਾਥ ਬਿਦੇਸ ਸਿਧਾਰੋ ॥
848.t: taa ko naath bidhes sidhaaro ||

849.g: ਤਿਹ ਜਿਯ ਸੋਕ ਤਵਨ ਕੌ ਭਾਰੋ ॥੨॥
849.t: teh jiy sok tavan kau bhaaro ||2||
849.e: Her husband had departed for a foreign land which gave her a big shock.(2)
Dohira

849.g: ਅਮਿਤ ਦਰਬ ਤਾ ਕੇ ਸਦਨ ਚੋਰਨ ਸੁਨੀ ਸੁਧਾਰਿ ॥
849.t: amit dharab taa ke sadhan choran sunee sudhaar ||
849.e: When thieves learned that she had lot of wealth at her house,

849.g: ਰੈਨਿ ਪਰੀ ਤਾ ਕੇ ਪਰੇ ਅਮਿਤ ਮਸਾਲੈ ਜਾਰਿ ॥੩॥
849.t: rain paree taa ke pare amit masaalai jaar ||3||
849.e: They took torches and headed towards her house.(3)
Chaupaee
When she saw the thieves coming, she said,
‘Listen, you, I am your woman, and considering as your own, protect me.(4)
Dohira

849.g: ਸਭ ਗ੍ਰਿਹ ਕੋ ਧਨੁ ਤੁਮ ਹਰਹੁ ਹਮਹੂੰ ਸੰਗ ਲੈ ਜਾਹੁ ॥
849.t: sabh gireh ko dhan tum harahu hamahoo(n) sa(n)g lai jaahu ||
849.e: ‘You can steel everything from the house and take me with you as weIl,

849.g: ਭਾਤਿ ਭਾਤਿ ਕੇ ਰੈਨਿ ਦਿਨ ਮੋ ਸੌ ਕੇਲ ਕਮਾਹੁ ॥੫॥
849.t: bhaat bhaat ke rain dhin mo sau kel kamaahu ||5||
849.e: ‘And, in numerous ways, enjoy with me.(5)

849.g: ਪ੍ਰਥਮ ਹਮਾਰੇ ਧਾਮ ਕੋ ਭੋਜਨ ਕਰਹੁ ਬਨਾਇ ॥
849.t: pratham hamaare dhaam ko bhojan karahu banai ||
849.e: ‘First I will prepare meals for you in my house,

849.g: ਪਾਛੇ ਮੁਹਿ ਲੈ ਜਾਇਯਹੁ ਹ੍ਰਿਦੈ ਹਰਖ ਉਪਜਾਇ ॥੬॥
849.t: paachhe muh lai jaiyahu hiradhai harakh upajai ||6||
849.e: ‘And then take me with you and savour me heart fully’.(6)
Chaupaee
The thieves thought that she was right, she was their own.
‘First we have meals and then let her become our woman.’(7)
Dohira

849.g: ਚੌਛਤਾ ਪਰ ਤਬ ਤਰੁਨਿ ਚੋਰਨ ਦਿਯੌ ਚਰਾਇ ॥
849.t: chauachhataa par tab tarun choran dhiyau charai ||
849.e: The woman sent the thieves to upstairs,

849.g: ਆਪਿ ਕਰਾਹੀ ਚਾਰਿ ਕੈ ਲੀਨੇ ਬਰੇ ਪਕਾਇ ॥੮॥
849.t: aap karaahee chaar kai leene bare pakai ||8||
849.e: And herself, putting the saucepan on fire, commenced cooking.(8)
Chaupaee
After sending them up in the pent-house, she came down and locked the door behind
After sending them up in the pent-house, she came down and locked the door behind
She, then settled down to prepare the meal and put poison in that.(9)
Dohira

849.g: ਡਾਰਿ ਮਹੁਰਾ ਭੋਜ ਮੈ ਚੋਰਨ ਦਯੋ ਖਵਾਇ ॥
849.t: ddaar mahuraa bhoj mai choran dhayo khavai ||
849.e: With poison in she presented meal to the thieves,

849.g: ਨਿਕਸਿ ਆਪਿ ਆਵਤ ਭਈ ਤਾਲੋ ਦ੍ਰਿੜ ਕਰਿ ਲਾਇ ॥੧੦॥
849.t: nikas aap aavat bhiee taalo dhiraR kar lai ||10||
849.e: And herself locked the door and came down.(10)
Chaupaee

849.g: ਹਸਿ ਹਸਿ ਬੈਨ ਚੋਰ ਸੋ ਕਹੈ ॥
849.t: has has bain chor so kahai ||

849.g: ਤਾ ਕੋ ਹਾਥ ਹਾਥ ਸੋ ਗਹੈ ॥
849.t: taa ko haath haath so gahai ||
849.e: (To leader of the thieves who was in the kitchen) She talked to him jovially by giving her hand in his.
(To leader of the thieves who was in the kitchen) She talked to him jovially by giving her hand in his.
She gave him pleasure through her talks while she put oil (on fire) to boil.(11)
Dohira

849.g: ਤੇਲ ਜਬੈ ਤਾਤੋ ਭਯੋ ਤਾ ਕੀ ਦ੍ਰਿਸਟਿ ਬਚਾਇ ॥
849.t: tel jabai taato bhayo taa kee dhirasaT bachai ||
849.e: When the oil was hot enough, with stealthy looks,

849.g: ਡਾਰਿ ਸੀਸ ਤਾ ਕੇ ਦਯੋ ਮਾਰਿਯੋ ਚੋਰ ਜਰਾਇ ॥੧੨॥
849.t: ddaar sees taa ke dhayo maariyo chor jarai ||12||
849.e: She dumped it on his head and thus killed him.(12)

849.g: ਚੋਰ ਰਾਜ ਜਰਿ ਕੈ ਮਰਿਯੋ ਚੋਰ ਮਰਿਯੋ ਬਿਖੁ ਖਾਇ ॥
849.t: chor raaj jar kai mariyo chor mariyo bikh khai ||
849.e: The leader of the thieves was killed with the boiling oil and others died of eating poison.

849.g: ਪ੍ਰਾਤ ਭਏ ਕੁਟਵਾਰ ਕੇ ਸਭ ਹੀ ਦਏ ਬੰਧਾਇ ॥੧੩॥
849.t: praat bhe kuTavaar ke sabh hee dhe ba(n)dhai ||13||
849.e: In the morning she went and related the whole story to (he chief of the police.(l3)(1)

849.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰ ਪਖ੍ਯਾਨੇ ਤ੍ਰਿਯਾ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰੋ ਮੰਤ੍ਰੀ ਭੂਪ ਸੰਬਾਦੇ ਬਤੀਸਵੋ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰ ਸਮਾਪਤਮ ਸਤੁ ਸੁਭਮ ਸਤੁ ॥੩੨॥੬੧੮॥ਅਫਜੂੰ॥
849.t: eit sree charitr pakhayaane tirayaa charitro ma(n)tree bhoop sa(n)baadhe bateesavo charitr samaapatam sat subham sat ||32||618||afajoo(n)||
849.e: Thirty-second Parable of Auspicious Chritars Conversation of the Raja and the Minister, Completed with Benediction. (32)(618)
Chaupaee

849.g: ਅਧਿਕ ਰੂਪ ਜਾ ਕੋ ਜਗ ਲਹਿਯੈ ॥
849.t: adhik roop jaa ko jag lahiyai ||
849.e: In. the North of the country, there lived a Raja who was very handsome.
His name was Chhattar Ket and, on seeing him, his wife always felt satiated.(1)
His name was Chhattar Ket and, on seeing him, his wife always felt satiated.(1)

849.g: ਅਧਿਕ ਰੂਪ ਜਗ ਸੁਨਤ ਜਵਨ ਕੋ ॥
849.t: adhik roop jag sunat javan ko ||
849.e: Her name was Chhattar Manjri; she was admired as the most beautiful.

850.e: Raja Chhattar Ket’s wife was so well known that she was famous in all the ten regions.(2)
Chhattar Manjri was so loveable that her features were much more attractive than the Raja’s.
Chhattar Manjri was so loveable that her features were much more attractive than the Raja’s.
She always pondered over, how their rule could remain dynamic for ever,(3)

850.g: ਕੰਨ੍ਯਾ ਹ੍ਵੈ ਤਾ ਕੇ ਮਰਿ ਜਾਹੀ ॥
850.t: ka(n)nayaa havai taa ke mar jaahee ||
850.e: She always pondered over, how their rule could remain dynamic for ever,(3)
Because her female issues would not survive, and had no luck of a son.

850.g: ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਕੌ ਸੋਕ ਅਧਿਕ ਜਿਯ ਭਾਰੋ ॥
850.t: tiray kau sok adhik jiy bhaaro ||

850.e: Her mind was very much inflicted and she thought of performing some unique exploit.(4) .

850.g: ਸੁਤ ਬਿਨੁ ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਚਿਤ ਚਿਤ ਬਿਚਾਰੀ ॥
850.t: sut bin tiray chit chit bichaaree ||
850.e: Her mind was very much inflicted and she thought of performing some unique exploit.(4) .

850.g: ਕ੍ਯੋ ਨ ਦੈਵ ਗਤਿ ਕਰੀ ਹਮਾਰੀ ॥
850.t: kayo na dhaiv gat karee hamaaree ||
850.e: She contemplated in her mind, ‘Not even God would approve me without a son,

850.g: ਦਿਜ ਮੁਰਿ ਹਾਥ ਦਾਨ ਨਹਿ ਲੇਹੀ ॥
850.t: dhij mur haath dhaan neh lehee ||
850.e: She contemplated in her mind, ‘Not even God would approve me without a son,
‘And Brahmins (priests) would not accept alms through my hands and populace would taunt me.(5)
‘And Brahmins (priests) would not accept alms through my hands and populace would taunt me.(5)
‘I should undertake some unworthy action and provide a son to the Raja.

850.g: ਨ੍ਰਿਪ ਕੋ ਕਵਨ ਨਿਰਖਿ ਹੈ ਆਈ ॥੬॥
850.t: nirap ko kavan nirakh hai aaiee ||6||
850.e: ‘I must manage to get a boy when the Raja comes to visit me,’(6)
The Raja, on the other hand, had retained a kept-woman, and spread the rum our of his second marriage.
The Raja, on the other hand, had retained a kept-woman, and spread the rum our of his second marriage.
The Rani was very much distressed and started to splurge the money out on her maids.(7)
Dohira

850.g: ਸਵਤਿ ਤ੍ਰਾਸ ਰਾਨੀ ਅਧਿਕ ਲੋਗਨ ਦਰਬੁ ਲੁਟਾਇ ॥
850.t: savat traas raanee adhik logan dharab luTai ||
850.e: Petrified of the co-wife, she started to squander wealth among people,

850.g: ਤੇ ਵਾ ਕੀ ਸਵਤਿਹ ਚਹੈ ਸਕੈ ਨ ਮੂਰਖ ਪਾਇ ॥੮॥
850.t: te vaa kee savateh chahai sakai na moorakh pai ||8||
850.e: But people still liked her co-wife and this fool could not acquiesce.(8)
Chaupaee

850.g: ਲੋਗ ਸਵਤਿ ਤਾ ਕੀ ਕਹ ਚਹੈ ॥
850.t: log savat taa kee keh chahai ||

850.g: ਵਾ ਕੀ ਉਸਤਤਿ ਨ੍ਰਿਪ ਸੋ ਕਹੈ ॥
850.t: vaa kee usatat nirap so kahai ||
850.e: People fancied her co-wife; they were full of her praise in the presence of the Raja. .

850.g: ਕਹੈ ਜੁ ਇਹ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਬਰੈ ਸੁ ਮਾਰੋ ॥
850.t: kahai ju ieh prabhoo barai su maaro ||
850.e: People fancied her co-wife; they were full of her praise in the presence of the Raja. .
She wanted Raja to eradicate her so that she could live happily.(9)

850.g: ਤਾ ਕੋ ਮੂੰਡ ਮੂੰਡ ਕਰਿ ਖਾਵੈ ॥
850.t: taa ko moo(n)dd moo(n)dd kar khaavai ||
850.e: The dread of the co-wife always haunted her, and she always craved to annihilate her,

850.g: ਤਾ ਕਹ ਦਰਬੁ ਨ ਦੇਖਨ ਦੇਹੀ ॥
850.t: taa keh dharab na dhekhan dhehee ||
850.e: The dread of the co-wife always haunted her, and she always craved to annihilate her,
She would not let money pass to her and plunder it when it was on its way to her (co-wife).(10)

850.g: ਪੁਨਿ ਤਿਹ ਮਿਲਿਹਿ ਸਵਤਿ ਸੌ ਜਾਈ ॥
850.t: pun teh mileh savat sau jaiee ||
850.e: She would not let money pass to her and plunder it when it was on its way to her (co-wife).(10)
But she used to meet the co-wife as well and often praised her saying,

850.g: ਤੁਮ ਕਹ ਬਰਿ ਹੈ ਨ੍ਰਿਪਤਿ ਹਮਾਰੋ ॥
850.t: tum keh bar hai nirapat hamaaro ||

850.e: ‘Our Raja will retain you and your magnificence will flourish.’(11)

850.g: ਯੌ ਕਹਿ ਕੈ ਤਾ ਕੌ ਧਨ ਲੂਟਹਿ ॥
850.t: yau keh kai taa kau dhan looTeh ||

850.g: ਬਹੁਰਿ ਆਨਿ ਵਾ ਤ੍ਰਿਯਾ ਕਹ ਕੂਟਹਿ ॥
850.t: bahur aan vaa tirayaa keh kooTeh ||
850.e: Outwardly she robbed her of her wealth and beat her (mentally).
Advancing in such a way, she ransacked them both lavishly.(12)
Dohira

850.g: ਅਨਿਕ ਭਾਤਿ ਤਿਹ ਨ੍ਰਿਪਤਿ ਕੋ ਦੁਹੂੰਅਨ ਤ੍ਰਾਸ ਦਿਖਾਇ ॥
850.t: anik bhaat teh nirapat ko dhuhoo(n)an traas dhikhai ||
850.e: Thus, both of them, as a matter of fact, indulged in many deceits,

850.g: ਦਰਬੁ ਜੜਨਿ ਕੇ ਧਾਮ ਕੌ ਇਹ ਛਲ ਛਲਹਿ ਬਨਾਇ ॥੧੩॥
850.t: dharab jaRan ke dhaam kau ieh chhal chhaleh banai ||13||
850.e: As they ravaged the Raja’s wealth through trickery.(l3)
Chaupaee
She had been laundering money foolishly and indulging in base action

851.g: ਅਧਿਕ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਤਿਨ ਕੇ ਸੰਗ ਠਾਨੈ ॥
851.t: adhik preet tin ke sa(n)g Thaanai ||

851.e: She loved many shady characters who could not understand this foolish woman.(14)
Dohira

851.g: ਤੇ ਰਮਿ ਔਰਨ ਸੋ ਕਹੈ ਇਹ ਕੁਤਿਯਾ ਕਿਹ ਕਾਜ ॥
851.t: te ram aauaran so kahai ieh kutiyaa keh kaaj ||
851.e: She would make love with others but denounced her co-wife as bitch.

851.g: ਏਕ ਦਰਬੁ ਹਮੈ ਚਾਹਿਯੈ ਜੌ ਦੈ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਜਦੁਰਾਜ ॥੧੫॥
851.t: ek dharab hamai chaahiyai jau dhai sree jadhuraaj ||15||
851.e: And the openly declared that she just wanted one son, which God would give her.(15)
Chaupaee

851.g: ਯਹ ਸਭ ਭੇਦ ਨ੍ਰਿਪਤਿ ਜਿਯ ਜਾਨੈ ॥
851.t: yeh sabh bhedh nirapat jiy jaanai ||

851.e: The Raja in fact knew all these happenings but the foolish woman had not discerned.
The Raja in fact knew all these happenings but the foolish woman had not discerned.
The Raja himself used to invite many other ladies to make love with them.(16)
Dohira

851.g: ਧ੍ਰਿਗ ਤਾ ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਕਹ ਭਾਖਿਯੈ ਜਾ ਕਹ ਪਿਯ ਨ ਬੁਲਾਇ ॥
851.t: dhirag taa tiray keh bhaakhiyai jaa keh piy na bulai ||
851.e: The woman, whose husband does not invite her into bed, is ill-fated.

851.g: ਤਿਹ ਦੇਖਤ ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਅਨਤ ਕੀ ਸੇਜ ਬਿਹਾਰਨ ਜਾਇ ॥੧੭॥
851.t: teh dhekhat tiray anat kee sej bihaaran jai ||17||
851.e: And the man, whose wife adores the bed of another person, is hapless.(17)
Chaupaee
The foolish (Rani) did not care and kept on squandering the wealth.
